meta.notes: Seed prices are unverified editorial estimates. Run a price refresh before going to press.

bikes.description: The Ninja is a full-on supersport bike, but its extra capacity and compliant chassis makes it far easier on the road than some rivals. And it's much better value than the new model!
bikes.notes: Bennetts quotes £6000-9000 for 2013-2021; trimmed to our 2013-2020 span

bikes.description: The bike that reminded everyone that cheap and light beats expensive and heavy. The CP2 twin is all torque and character, the chassis is willing, and running costs are close to trivial. Budget suspension is the only real giveaway.
bikes.notes: Bennetts £3000-6500 covers to 2024; 2014-2020 sits in the lower band

bikes.description: The default sensible first big bike, and none the worse for it. A2-legal, unburstable, and cheap to insure. Nobody ever fell in love with one, but nobody ever got let down by one either.
bikes.notes: Derived from the CB500X guide (£2500-6799); F trades slightly below X

bikes.description: Suzuki went back to the original recipe and got it right. The V-twin has proper mid-range, the bike is narrow and easy, and the used market is deep enough that you can afford to be fussy.
cons: Suspension is built to a price
bikes.notes: Bennetts headline range

bikes.description: Still the benchmark middleweight naked. The triple gives you the low-down of a twin and the top end of a four, and the chassis flatters everyone. R models get the better brakes and suspension and are worth chasing.
cons: regulator/rectifier is a known weak spot
bikes.notes: Bennetts headline; R models c.£500 more

bikes.description: Wildly entertaining and slightly unhinged, especially in early form. The triple is a gem. Early bikes need the suspension sorting before you can trust the front end, and plenty already have been.
A proper little hooligan that happens to be A2 legal. Sharp chassis, strong brakes and an engine that revs hard. Build quality is the compromise, and service intervals come round quickly.

The most complete 600 of its generation and the one that will still be running when the others aren't. Docile at road pace, ferocious above 10,000rpm, and screwed together to a standard rivals didn't match.
The sharpest tool in the 600 box and the one that flatters a track day most. Utterly uninterested in anything below 8,000rpm, which is either the point or the problem depending on your commute.
The one everybody says they should have bought, and they're right. 600 chassis, near-litre grunt, and no direct rival left on the market. Values have stopped falling, so buy sooner rather than later.
cons: no rider aids to speak of
bikes.notes: Bennetts headline range

bikes.description: The bike that made every other superbike feel a generation behind overnight. Still savagely quick, still loaded with electronics, and now available for middleweight money. Check the service history obsessively.
A lot of motorcycle for the money. Smooth, strong four-cylinder, sensible ergonomics and enough presence to feel special. The 2020 update added the electronics the early bikes go without.
bikes.notes: Editorial £6800-£9800

bikes.description: All the Monster attitude with none of the belt-service anxiety of the older air-cooled bikes. Sounds terrific, looks better, and is far more usable than its reputation suggests. Just budget for Ducati servicing.
bikes.notes: Bennetts £4500-10000 across both generations

bikes.description: The default big adventure bike and still the one to beat. The liquid-cooled boxer is stronger and smoother than the oil-cooled bike it replaced, and it will cross continents without complaint. Options list dictates value enormously.
cons: spec variation makes pricing a minefield
bikes.notes: Guide covers 2004-2019 at £3800-10500; LC sits in the upper half

bikes.description: The adventure bike for people who actually go off road. Lighter and more willing in the dirt than the German opposition, if noticeably down on power. DCT versions are better than the purists will admit.
cons: Down on power for the class

bikes.description: A middleweight adventure bike with a proper triple soundtrack. The XC gets wire wheels and longer travel, the XR is the better road bike. Comfortable, capable and usually cheaper than the obvious alternatives.
bikes.notes: Bennetts £4000-6000 for 2011-14; later XRx up to £7500

bikes.description: MT-09 engine, sensible bodywork, and suddenly you have one of the most useful bikes on sale. Quick enough to entertain, practical enough to commute, and the GT version adds panniers and heated grips as standard.
bikes.notes: 2015 from £4500; updated bike £6500-7500

bikes.description: Not glamorous, endlessly competent. The ER-6 twin is willing, the riding position is spot on for long days, and it will shrug off a British winter better than most. An underrated do-everything bike.

The thinking rider's sports tourer, and cheap now in a way it won't stay. Gear-driven cams, that V4 noise, and the ability to do 500 miles without fuss. Check for regulator/rectifier and rear shock work.
cons: reg/rec is a known failure point
bikes.notes: Bennetts £2000-5500; late bikes with luggage near £4000

bikes.description: A long-stroke K5 GSX-R1000 motor in a comfortable naked chassis, sold for sensible money. Brutally effective and rather overlooked, which is exactly why it's such good used value.
bikes.notes: Guide £4500-8500 incl. F and later bikes

bikes.description: The liquid-cooled Bonnie kept the looks and lost the vagueness. Torquey, beautifully finished and easy to ride slowly, which is mostly what you'll want to do on it. Accessory catalogue is a money pit.
bikes.notes: Widened after dealer cross-check: Webbs/CMC hold T100s at £7499-£10195, above our previous £7300 top

bikes.description: More fashion statement than dirt bike, but a thoroughly likeable one. The air-cooled twin has plenty of character, it's light and low, and it makes a fine second bike. Don't take the knobbly-tyre styling literally.
bikes.notes: £4500 private, £5000-5500 dealer; variants fetch more

bikes.description: Bought with the heart, and there's nothing wrong with that. Looks and sounds the part, and the aftermarket will let you change everything else. Just don't expect it to corner, stop or tour.
bikes.notes: Early bikes c.£5000; tidy 2013 £5500-6000. Values very sticky

bikes.description: A proper inline four in a class full of twins, and all the better for it. Revs sweetly, looks sharp in Neo Sports Cafe trim, and carries Honda's usual build quality. A grown-up alternative to an MT-07.
Sportsbike looks with a commuter's manners. The parallel twin is flexible and frugal, the riding position is far kinder than the fairing suggests, and it makes a sound first full-licence bike.
bikes.notes: Guide £3500-8000 includes near-new; 2017-2023 sits lower

bikes.description: The bike that reinvented the sporty middleweight. Light, clever, loaded with electronics and fast enough anywhere you'd legally use it. Depreciation has been kind to buyers and brutal to first owners.
bikes.notes: 2021-22 with 11-13k miles c.£7295; 2025 low-mileage c.£9495. Good examples sell fast

bikes.description: The scalpel of the middleweight naked class. Brembo Stylema brakes, proper suspension and a punchy twin that never stops pulling. Uncompromising in a way that will delight some and exhaust others.
bikes.notes: Fast Bikes quotes £4999-£6300 for 2020-2022; our top covers later bikes

bikes.description: The last of the 1050s and the best of them. Ohlins, Brembos and a triple that sounds like nothing else. Heavier than the newest super nakeds but with a character they can't match.
bikes.notes: Guide £8000-12500 for S and RS; RS from c.£9000

bikes.description: Deeply sensible and quietly brilliant at the job it was designed for. 70mpg, a boot where the tank should be, and torque exactly where you use it. Nobody's dream bike, everybody's useful one.
bikes.notes: Little under £4000 at the bottom; late low-mile bikes £4500+

bikes.description: An MT-07 in a better suit. Same superb CP2 twin, same low weight, but with retro detailing that has aged well. Often cheaper than the equivalent MT because fewer people think to look for one.
bikes.notes: Clean examples from just over £3000

bikes.description: The bike that invented the superbike, by then grown comfortable in middle age. The F2 is heavier and softer than the original but far easier to live with, and the four-into-one howl is intact. Values have quietly firmed up while nobody was looking.
bikes.notes: 1983 FA c.£2950, 1980 FB sold £5750, minter with UK provenance £7989

bikes.description: Six cylinders, twenty-four valves and a noise like nothing else on the road. Absurd then, magnificent now. Wide, heavy and thirsty, but you don't buy one of these to be sensible — you buy it to hear it.
bikes.notes: Market average c.£13.4k; auction comparable £7475. UK investment-grade examples scarce

bikes.description: Honda's first serious V4 sportster, and the one that taught them a hard lesson about camshafts. Sort the top end and it's a lovely thing — smooth, quick and better balanced than the inline fours it fought. Buy on engine history alone.
cons: Camshaft wear is the model's shadow
bikes.notes: Little UK data; US sales $2200-$7875 converted and adjusted

bikes.description: The homologation special that beat everything and still looks like it could. Hand-built, gear-driven cams, single-sided swingarm and a riding experience that flatters and terrifies in equal measure. The prices are silly. It's still worth it.
bikes.notes: Rough £15-19k, tidy £20-27k, mint £30-35k. £65k record is an outlier

bikes.description: The bike that defined the do-everything middleweight. Fast enough to embarrass sportsbikes, comfortable enough to tour, and so reliable that most survivors have been ridden into the ground. Finding a clean one is now the hard part.
bikes.notes: Editorial £1800-£3800; our £800 floor was implausibly low for a running example

bikes.description: Big, heavy and utterly unburstable. The CBR1000F will cross Europe two-up without breaking sweat and shrug off mileages that would frighten most bikes. Not remotely sporty by modern standards, and all the better for admitting it.
bikes.notes: Listings £900-£3199 by year and mileage

bikes.description: A two-stroke triple built to cash in on Freddie Spencer's title, and one of the most usable strokers ever sold. Less frantic than a Gamma, prettier than most, and increasingly collectable. A genuinely rideable classic race replica.
bikes.notes: Rough £4-5k, tidy £6-9k, mint £10-12k. £10k less than an RG500

bikes.description: A big thumper from the era when Honda still built simple things properly. Torquey, light and honest, with a lovely gearbox and enough character to forgive the modest performance. Increasingly popular as a cafe racer base.

Before adventure bikes got tall, heavy and expensive, there was the Transalp. Modest power, huge comfort and legendary reliability. It'll do green lanes, commutes and continents without ever feeling special — which is rather the point.
bikes.notes: UK/near-market listings £1255-£3895

bikes.description: The original Africa Twin, and to many the only one. Big, softly sprung and unstoppable, with a V-twin that pulls forever and a reputation for surviving anything. Values have woken up as the modern bike drew attention back to it.
bikes.notes: Editorial £4500-£8500; the original Africa Twin has appreciated sharply

bikes.description: The Elsie. Water-cooled, powerband-obsessed and responsible for more misspent youth than any bike before or since. Terrifying, addictive and now seriously collectable. Almost none are unmolested, so buy the history as much as the bike.
bikes.notes: Top 4L0 and YPVS examples £10-15k; broader market below that

bikes.description: A road-going V4 two-stroke built because Yamaha could. Brutal, peaky and utterly uncompromising, it remains one of the maddest things ever sold with a number plate. Ride one and the 1980s make perfect sense.
bikes.notes: Listings £17995-£21989; auctions £18975 and £17438, but one at £9281

bikes.description: Yamaha's five-valve experiment and a hugely underrated bike. Smooth, strong and far more comfortable than the race replicas it shared showrooms with. Still cheap, which won't last much longer.
bikes.notes: Good 1987 at £2400; fully restored UK bike £8495

bikes.description: The EXUP was the fastest thing on the road and felt it. That exhaust valve gave it midrange nothing else had, and the chassis was good enough to use it. A genuine landmark, and still shockingly rapid.
bikes.notes: Editorial £3000-£6000; ours was built from the rough end of the market

bikes.description: Shaft drive, an unburstable four and a riding position built for distance. The XJ900 was the sensible choice then and it's the bargain now — a proper big tourer for less than the price of a decent set of leathers.
bikes.notes: eBay and classifieds £550-£2390

bikes.description: Kick-start only, one cylinder, no pretence. The SR500 is a lesson in doing without, and it has become the default custom donor for exactly that reason. Learn the starting drill and it's tremendously satisfying.
bikes.notes: Imports from c.£1500; well-presented 1983 at £5989

bikes.description: Nothing rides like a V-Max. That V4 delivers a shove in the back that still shocks, wrapped in a chassis that never quite agreed with the idea. Utterly flawed, completely brilliant, and unlike anything else.
bikes.notes: Road-ready £3800-£5800; well-presented to £7300. Auction median £2415

bikes.description: A big, muscular sports tourer that has aged into a superb budget mile-eater. The motor is essentially unbreakable and the riding position works all day. Heavy, but that mass turns into stability once you're moving.
bikes.notes: Consistent £1500-£2500 across UK classifieds

bikes.description: The bike that started the race replica era. Oil-cooled, aluminium-framed and shockingly light, it made everything else look overweight overnight. Raw, demanding and now firmly collectable.
bikes.notes: 1987 slabside auction £3335; clean 1985-89 bikes reach £9-10k+

bikes.description: All the GSX-R attitude with a great deal more shove. Fast in a straight line, entertaining everywhere else, and famous for flexing when provoked. A brutal, honest superbike from before electronics smoothed the edges.
bikes.notes: Projects £3.5-5k, roadworthy £6.5-9k, restored £10-14k

bikes.description: A square-four two-stroke built for the road because Suzuki wanted to prove a point. Light, savage and wonderfully unhinged, it's the closest most of us will get to a GP bike. Prices reflect that.
bikes.notes: Listings £9995-£21500; tidy examples the fat end of £20k. Auction £24725

bikes.description: Styling that outraged everyone in 1981 and looks magnificent now. The Katana was a proper fast bike underneath the drama, and it has become one of the most desirable Japanese classics of the era.
bikes.notes: Typical £5500-£7500, needs-work c.£4300, minter c.£10k. Auction £4715

bikes.description: The first modern superbike, and the one Top Gun made famous. Liquid-cooled, sixteen valves and genuinely quick, yet civil enough to tour on. Still a lovely thing to ride and finally getting the recognition it deserves.
bikes.notes: Editorial list quotes £4500-£9500 for good examples; our floor stays, top raised

bikes.description: The first of the modern 600s and the bike that created the class. Quick, sharp and hugely successful in its day, though most have long since rusted away. A tidy one is a genuine piece of history.
bikes.notes: Few complete examples listed; mostly projects. Project seen at £800

bikes.description: Those hoover pipes, that green and white paint, and a race-bred chassis that flattered everyone. The ZXR was Kawasaki taking the 750 class seriously, and it's now a proper period icon.
bikes.notes: Listings £2799-£12000; good examples from c.£2k, most £3250-£4500

bikes.description: Six cylinders, shaft drive and nearly 300kg of unapologetic excess. The Z1300 is absurd in the best way, smoother than anything has a right to be, and increasingly sought after by people who like their bikes enormous.
bikes.notes: Most usable examples £5-10k; 1979 listed £8495

bikes.description: The bike that invented the adventure class. Light, simple and monumentally capable, with the Paris-Dakar wins to prove it. Every GS since traces back to this, and values have followed that story upward.
bikes.notes: Typical £5500-£9500; sound usable classics £7000-£12000

bikes.description: The flying brick. A longitudinal four laid on its side, shaft drive and a reputation for covering enormous distances without complaint. Odd-looking, deeply competent, and a bargain way into old BMW ownership.
bikes.notes: £1000-£2000 typical, good ones to £3000. Café racer demand firming values

bikes.description: The first production bike with a factory-developed full fairing, and still a beautiful thing. The boxer twin is unhurried and characterful, and the wind protection genuinely works. A classic that you can actually use.
bikes.notes: Road-ready £5000-£9500; UK average £5600-£9000, restored £10k+

bikes.description: The bike that launched Ducati's superbike dynasty. Liquid-cooled, four-valve and fuel-injected when that was exotic, it turned a struggling firm into a world championship force. Fragile, gorgeous, historically vital.
bikes.notes: Typical 1989-91 £7000-£12500, most around £10k. SP variants far higher

bikes.description: A transverse V-twin, shaft drive and a riding position that means business. The Le Mans is more about feel than pace — it rumbles, it leans, and it makes every journey an occasion. Italian character with German solidity.
bikes.notes: Auction £5635; fully restored 1977 listed £18500

bikes.description: Loud, fast and gloriously unreasonable. The Jota was among the quickest bikes of its day and remains one of the most charismatic triples ever built. Not for the faint-hearted, then or now.
bikes.notes: Bonhams 1981 Jota 180 £7705; 1980 listed £16000. Early 180s worth most

bikes.description: The end of the old Meriden line, and a bike best judged on charm rather than engineering. Get one that has been properly sorted and it's a delight; get a neglected one and you'll learn more about oil leaks than you wanted.
bikes.notes: Private from £5000, dealers £6-8k for mint. Auction median £3047

bikes.description: The Isolastic engine mounts made the Commando smoother than it had any right to be, and the shape is among the prettiest ever drawn. A proper British classic that rewards a sympathetic owner.
bikes.notes: Listings £4950-£9995; excellent 1973 Roadster £9950

bikes.description: The Harley that actually handles. The FXR's rubber-mounted frame gave it composure the Softails never had, and it has become the connoisseur's choice. Prices have climbed as that reputation spread.
bikes.notes: Editorial quotes £8500-£15000 for the FXRT; FXR values have climbed hard

bikes.description: Before the Wing became a six-cylinder sofa it was a flat four, and rather more of a motorcycle for it. Comfortable, smooth and hugely capable over distance, and now a cheap way into serious touring.
bikes.notes: 1983 sold at auction £4025; 1980 listed c.£2000

bikes.description: Suzuki's answer to the Paris-Dakar boom, and a bike far better known on the continent than here. Big, tall and single-cylinder, with genuine off-road ability and an appealingly odd shape.
bikes.notes: Still no UK-specific data found; US-derived figure retained and flagged

bikes.description: A two-stroke twin in a supermoto-before-supermoto chassis. Odd-looking, wildly entertaining and now a proper cult bike. Light enough to flick anywhere and fast enough to get you in trouble.
bikes.notes: Editorial £4500-£8000; cult two-stroke demand is firm

bikes.description: The despatch rider's friend. Shaft drive, an unburstable four and absolutely no glamour whatsoever. Thousands of them covered astronomical mileages, which is exactly why so few remain tidy.
bikes.notes: 1987 at £795, excellent 1988 at £2000

bikes.description: A neat, willing middleweight four from Suzuki's most dependable era. Not fast, but beautifully made and endlessly tuneable, which is why so many became café racers. A sensible first classic.
bikes.notes: Restoration projects from a few hundred; tidy examples to £3250

bikes.description: A big, handsome four from the tail end of the UJM era, with more muscle than the CB750 and a name borrowed from endurance racing. Comfortable, quick enough and increasingly appreciated.
bikes.notes: Tidy standard under £1000 at the bottom; 1981-85 listings £2755-£6889

bikes.description: The big thumper that won the first Paris-Dakar and launched a thousand desert fantasies. Simple, light and full of character, with a kick-start ritual that becomes part of the appeal.
bikes.notes: Listings £4999-£10206; auctions £4025 and £6670. Auction median £3565

bikes.description: The bike that rewrote the rules. Tadao Baba's insight was simple — build a 900 that weighed what a 600 did — and it made every rival obsolete overnight. Twitchy, urgent and utterly thrilling. Early 893s are now serious collectables.
bikes.notes: Editorial £4500-£9500; early 1992 bikes now carry collector money

bikes.description: The middleweight everyone learned on, raced and toured. The F-series balanced pace and practicality better than anything else and sold in enormous numbers. Reliability is legendary; rust is the only real enemy.

Gear-driven cams, a V4 howl and Honda build quality at its absolute peak. The VFR750 is arguably the most complete motorcycle ever made — fast enough, comfortable enough, and nearly impossible to break.
bikes.notes: UK listings £895-£2599; condition and extras matter more than year

bikes.description: A CBR600 motor in a stripped-back chassis, sold cheap. The Hornet was a masterstroke — fast, flickable and endlessly entertaining, with a scream at the top end that naked bikes rarely offer.
bikes.notes: Guide £1500-£2750 by year; 1998 private £1500, 2006 dealer £2750

bikes.description: Honda's V-twin answer to the Ducati question. Torquey, characterful and easier to live with than the Italian alternative, if never quite as sharp. Tiny fuel range is the one real gripe.
bikes.notes: Tatty from just over £1000; good early £1900-2500, later big-tank £3000-3500

bikes.description: Built to take the top-speed crown and civilised enough to tour on afterwards. The Blackbird is astonishingly smooth, effortlessly fast and screwed together to a standard that shames most modern bikes.
bikes.notes: Anything with an MOT makes £2500; low-mileage later bikes near £4000

bikes.description: A big single trail bike that became the despatch rider's weapon of choice. Simple, tough and light enough to enjoy, with just enough off-road ability to be useful. A superb basis for a scrambler build.
bikes.notes: Realistic band £2000-£3750, recent data clustering low-to-mid £3000s

bikes.description: The FireBlade's nemesis. Yamaha stacked the gearbox to shorten the engine, wrapped it in a Deltabox frame and produced something that felt like a 600 with 150bhp. A genuine landmark, and still intoxicating.
bikes.notes: Editorial £5000-£11000; early R1s now carry collector money

bikes.description: The first R6 revved to the moon and looked spectacular doing it. Sharp, light and utterly uninterested in low revs, it defined the modern supersport 600 alongside the R1's litre-class revolution.
bikes.notes: Editorial £2800-£5500

bikes.description: The EXUP's replacement, overshadowed at launch by the R1 and rather good in its own right. Strong, stable and comfortable, it makes a superb budget fast tourer for people who don't need the last word in sharpness.
Yamaha's Ducati tribute, complete with trellis frame and a 270-degree crank that gave it the twin-cylinder character everyone wanted. A cult bike now, and deservedly so.
bikes.notes: Listings £2521-£3995; still cheap for a cult bike

bikes.description: Air-cooled, four-cylinder and utterly honest. The XJR is a muscle bike from an earlier age that Yamaha kept building because people kept buying it. Ohlins shocks as standard on later bikes are a nice touch.
bikes.notes: Carb bikes from c.£3999; late old-style just under £6000 at a dealer

bikes.description: Thunderace brakes, an R6-derived motor and a price that undercut everything. The Fazer was the sensible enthusiast's choice and remains one of the great used bargains. Rust is the only serious issue.
bikes.notes: Poor examples c.£600; tidy 2003 in a dealer c.£2500-£2700

bikes.description: Neither road bike nor trail bike, and better than that sounds. The TDM's parallel twin has real character and the upright riding position works everywhere. Odd, likeable and cheap.

The definition of unremarkable, and a superb bike for exactly that reason. Cheap, reliable and forgiving, the Diversion taught thousands of riders their trade. Nobody's dream bike, everyone's sensible one.
bikes.notes: Cheap end of the market; higher listings are the later XJ6, not the Diversion

bikes.description: Air-cooled, simple and endlessly cheerful. The Bandit 600 sold by the container-load because it did everything adequately for very little money, and a tidy one is still one of the best-value bikes going.
An oil-cooled GSX-R-derived motor in a basic chassis for pocket money. The Bandit 1200 is a hooligan's bargain — torquey, tough and capable of embarrassing far pricier machinery.
bikes.notes: 1999 high-miler £1750 up to £3500 for a low-mileage 2005

bikes.description: Suzuki's V-twin, complete with the rotary rear damper that gave it a fearsome reputation. Sort the suspension and it's a fast, characterful thing. Leave it standard and it'll keep you honest.
bikes.notes: Editorial £3200-£6500

bikes.description: Light, sharp and thoroughly race-focused, the SRAD was Suzuki taking the 600 class seriously. Fragile electrics and a hard life for most survivors mean condition matters more than mileage.
bikes.notes: Editorial £2200-£4500

bikes.description: The fastest production bike in the world, and shaped like nothing else before or since. Beneath the drama it's a surprisingly civilised long-distance machine with bottomless torque. An icon of excess.
bikes.notes: Tidy early bikes under £4000; unrestricted 1999-2000 bikes hold value best

bikes.description: Overlooked in period and a genuine bargain now. Strong, stable and comfortable, the RF900 is a fast tourer wearing sportsbike clothes. Its unfashionable shape keeps prices low.
bikes.notes: Poor early bikes from c.£700, nice 1999 c.£1200, dealer machines to £2500

bikes.description: For years the fastest thing you could buy, and still a monumentally capable long-distance weapon. The ZZR's ram-air motor is famously tough and the comfort is genuine. A lot of bike for very little money.
bikes.notes: Editorial £2800-£5500

bikes.description: Beautiful, heavy and gloriously stubborn. The ZX-7R was outclassed on paper by the time it hit its stride, but it steers with real authority and looks better than almost anything of its era.
bikes.notes: Typical £2500-£3500; 1996-2000 listings £2995-£3499. RR variants far rarer

bikes.description: The FireBlade's big-boned rival. Never as sharp, always faster in a straight line, and far more comfortable than the class demanded. Later C and E models are the ones to have.
bikes.notes: Good one under £3000; £2000-£2500 buys the widest choice. Dealer asks to £5000 are optimistic

bikes.description: A parallel twin commuter built to a price and beyond criticism at what it does. Thousands of riding schools bought them, which tells you everything about how tough they are.
bikes.notes: Searched but found no reliable UK price guide; figure retained from estimate

bikes.description: A better Bonneville than Triumph were building at the time, complete with bevel-driven cam and kick-start. Beautifully made, gentle to ride and now firmly collectable.
bikes.notes: Rougher/high-mileage approaching £3000, well-maintained above £4000. Customs far more

bikes.description: Twin headlights, a single-sided swingarm and the noise that made Triumph's name. The T509 turned the streetfighter idea into a proper production bike and still looks purposeful.
bikes.notes: Editorial £3200-£6500 for the T509/955i

bikes.description: Britain's answer to the Japanese superbike, with a triple that trades top-end scream for real-world drive. Comfortable for the class and increasingly appreciated as a usable modern classic.
bikes.notes: Clean examples from c.£2250; listings £1750 (41k miles) to £3955 (7k miles)

bikes.description: Hinckley's big tourer, built on the modular engine family and capable of enormous distances. Solid, comfortable and now extremely cheap for the amount of motorcycle involved.
bikes.notes: Older T300-era bikes at the cheap end; higher listings are the 2012-on Trophy

bikes.description: A retro built on modern underpinnings, and rather good for it. The triple gives it more urgency than the styling suggests, and Hinckley reliability means it's a classic you can actually rely on.
bikes.notes: Projects £1.8-2.8k, roadworthy £3.2-4.8k, collector-grade £5.5-7.5k. Sport 10-20% more

bikes.description: A big trailie with a triple, built when adventure bikes were still a niche. More road-biased than it looks, comfortable over distance, and increasingly sought after by people avoiding GS prices.
bikes.notes: Searched but found no reliable UK guide for 1993-2000; figure retained from estimate

bikes.description: Massimo Tamburini's masterpiece, and arguably the most beautiful motorcycle ever made. The underseat pipes, the single-sided swingarm, that noise — it won championships and hearts in equal measure.
bikes.notes: Editorial £10000-£22000. Our mid-market research stands, but the top was too low for good bikes

bikes.description: A 916 that asks you to work for it. Less torque, more revs, and a chassis every bit as good. For many riders it's the sweeter bike, and it has spent years in the 916's shadow price-wise.
bikes.notes: Baseline around £6000; SP with low miles over £8000. Service history worth c.£1000

bikes.description: Miguel Galluzzi took a trellis frame, an air-cooled twin and nothing else, and created a genre. The original Monster is raw, loud and still one of the best-looking naked bikes ever drawn.
bikes.notes: 2002 at £3209 up to £6998 for a 1999; 1993 auction estimate £4000-£6000

bikes.description: A Suzuki RGV250 motor in an Aprilia chassis with Max Biaggi's paint. The last of the road-going two-stroke sportsbikes and one of the most exciting things you can ride on a British B-road.
bikes.notes: Adverts cluster £9300-£14700; values have risen sharply since c.£7500 in 2019

bikes.description: A big single trailie with Italian styling and Austrian mechanicals. Charismatic and comfortable, but you'll want to check the service history closely — neglect shows up expensively.
bikes.notes: Sensible band £1300-£2300; listings £1195-£2995

bikes.description: The bike that turned the GS from a curiosity into an institution. Telelever front end, boxer torque and the ability to go absolutely anywhere. Ugly to some, magnificent to the faithful.
bikes.notes: From £2000 with 60k+ miles; £3000-£4000 buys under 40k. Good one c.£3500

bikes.description: A Rotax single in a friendly chassis, sold as the accessible BMW. Light enough for green lanes, comfortable enough for commuting, and famously hard to kill.
bikes.notes: Listings £750-£2495; a 2001 made £862 at auction

bikes.description: BMW's attempt at a sportsbike, which turned out to be a superb fast tourer instead. The boxer sounds wonderful, the build is excellent, and prices remain modest for what you get.
bikes.notes: Standard bikes £2500-£5000; Boxer Cup variants to £9000

bikes.description: A 125 that looks like a 916 and rides like a proper race bike. The Mito taught a generation how to use a powerband and remains the most exciting learner-legal bike ever built.
bikes.notes: Editorial £3500-£7000; Mito values have risen with two-stroke demand

bikes.description: The most sensible motorcycle ever made. Pushrod simplicity, legendary economy and the ability to survive total neglect. It taught half the country to ride and asked for nothing in return.
bikes.notes: Decent drum-brake bike c.£800, electric start c.£1200. Depreciation-proof

bikes.description: A GPZ500 twin in trail bike clothing. Not especially good at anything, but cheap, tough and comfortable enough to be genuinely useful. A budget adventure bike before that was a category.
bikes.notes: Search returns the unrelated 2026 KLE500; no usable data for the 1991-2007 bike

bikes.description: A proper trail bike that happened to be road legal. Light, willing and genuinely capable off road, which is why so many were ridden into the ground. Clean ones are increasingly hard to find.
bikes.notes: Can be had for under £1000; tidier examples to c.£2546

bikes.description: A huge naked four with FireBlade-derived power and presence to match. Heavy and thirsty, but the sheer physical scale of it is part of the appeal. A cult muscle bike.
bikes.notes: European comparables c.£1800-£3800; UK custom example at £3999

bikes.description: The FireBlade grown into a full litre bike, with MotoGP-derived styling and Honda's usual composure. Less frantic than rivals, easier to ride fast, and now remarkable value for a genuine superbike.
bikes.notes: Early examples £3000-£5000 on the classifieds; 2007 with 41k miles at £3490

bikes.description: The last of the small FireBlades and the one enthusiasts hunt down. Lighter than the 1000 that replaced it, savagely quick and beautifully balanced. A modern classic in the making.
bikes.notes: Listings £2990-£3500; tidy private sales upward of £4000, dealers near £5000

bikes.description: Honda doing sensible extremely well. Adjustable seat, upright bars, Hornet-derived motor and total dependability. It won't thrill you, but it will never let you down either.
bikes.notes: 2005-09 bikes £895-£2000; a tidy low-mileage 2006 c.£1900

bikes.description: A detuned FireBlade motor in a comfortable, practical chassis. The CBF1000 is one of the great overlooked tourers — quick enough, comfortable all day, and cheap because nobody talks about it.
bikes.notes: Listings £2995-£4998; 2010 models start c.£4000

bikes.description: A Firestorm V-twin in a big adventure chassis. Enormously comfortable and utterly unburstable, if far too heavy to take seriously off road. A superb budget continent-crosser.
bikes.notes: 1999 at £2500 up to £4299 for a 2008; later 2012-13 bikes higher still

bikes.description: The police force's choice, which tells you most of what you need to know. Vast, smooth, shaft-driven and capable of enormous mileages without complaint. Ex-police bikes are cheap for good reason.
bikes.notes: Early 2000s from £850-£3290; 2005-2011 £3300-£4950; dealers ask more

bikes.description: Built-in panniers, shaft drive and a complete absence of drama. The Deauville is transport rather than romance, and superb at it. Beloved of touring riders who've stopped caring what people think.
bikes.notes: 2006 with 34k miles £1500; low-mileage 2007 c.£3089

bikes.description: The R1 at its most focused. Underseat pipes, a chassis that finally matched the engine, and a top end that still feels ferocious. Widely regarded as the best-looking R1 of them all.
bikes.notes: 2004 with 35k miles £4695; 2006 with 23k miles £5340

bikes.description: An R6 motor detuned for the road in a practical half-faired chassis. Revvy, reliable and cheap, though the standard suspension and notorious rear-hugger corrosion need attention.
bikes.notes: High-mileage private £1500-£2000; tidy sub-20k c.£2500; dealer low-mileage c.£3500

bikes.description: An R1 engine in an upright chassis, which is exactly as good as it sounds. Immensely fast, comfortable enough for distance, and one of the great value fast bikes on the used market.
bikes.notes: High-mileage c.£2000; 20-30k miles £3000-£3500; a real beauty c.£4000

bikes.description: A 1700cc pushrod V-twin from a cruiser, dropped into a sportsbike chassis. Utterly bonkers, gloriously torquey and unlike anything else Yamaha has built. A cult bike with rising values.
bikes.notes: From £6000 at c.25k miles, pristine £8000-£9000. Scarcity keeps values firm

bikes.description: A big, tough single in supermoto or trail guise. Simple, light enough to enjoy and capable of shrugging off serious abuse. The X supermoto version is the one for road riders.
bikes.notes: Top nudged up: a 2013 with 6.2k miles at £5499

bikes.description: The TDM grown up. Still odd-looking, still hard to categorise, and still a superb real-world bike. The parallel twin has genuine character and the chassis is far better than the styling suggests.
bikes.notes: 2004 with 35k miles £2495; later low-mileage bikes to £4735 at a dealer

bikes.description: The K5 is the one. A motor so strong it became the default engine for streetfighters and drag bikes, wrapped in a chassis light enough to use it. Widely held to be the best superbike of its decade.
bikes.notes: K5-K6 rough £2500-3200, tidy £3600-4500, mint £5000-5500. Listings run above guide

bikes.description: The half-faired SV, and one of the great budget bikes. That V-twin has character the parallel twins can't match, the chassis is willing, and racing them is an entire subculture.
bikes.notes: Second-gen guide rough £1500-2000 to mint £3400-3800; first-gen sits below that

bikes.description: The thinking rider's adventure bike. SV650 reliability, upright comfort and enough ability to tackle a gravel track. Charmless to look at and beloved by everyone who owns one.
bikes.notes: Under £2500 available; budget £3000-£3500 for a nice sub-20k example

bikes.description: The bigger V-Strom, with TL1000 torque and the same practical bent. Heavier and thirstier than the 650 but far stronger, and just as tough. A superb budget tourer.
bikes.notes: 2002-08 bikes £2000-£3000 tidy with luggage; later ones higher

bikes.description: A GSX-R600 motor in a streetfighter chassis with aggressive styling. Fast enough and cheap, though the fuelling is abrupt and the finish suffers badly in British winters.
bikes.notes: 2006 with 18k miles £2689; 2007 with 6k miles £3990

bikes.description: Kawasaki's most aggressive superbike, and a bike with a reputation for biting. Savage top end, nervous chassis and enormous character. Later models tamed it, but the early ones are the exciting ones.
bikes.notes: Editorial £4200-£7800

bikes.description: A budget streetfighter that punched well above its price. Torquey, aggressive-looking and cheap to buy, though the suspension and brakes were built to a firm budget.
Four pipes, a mean stance and a motor derived from the ZX-9R. The Z1000 gave the naked class proper attitude and remains a lot of bike for the money.
bikes.notes: Editorial £4500-£9500 across the generation

bikes.description: A parallel twin naked built to be accessible, and quietly one of the best-judged bikes of its era. Light, forgiving and cheap, with just enough poke to stay interesting.
The Hayabusa's nemesis and a genuinely astonishing motorcycle. Effortlessly fast, remarkably smooth and comfortable enough for real distance. Enormous performance for very sensible money.
The W650's successor, with the same bevel-driven cam and beautiful detailing. Slower and gentler than its looks suggest, and all the more charming for it. Superb build quality.
bikes.notes: Over 20k miles c.£3000; sweet spot £4000-£5000 for sub-10k. 2016 with 10.7k miles £4995

bikes.description: The Speed Triple that got it right. More capacity, more character and that unmistakable triple bellow. Comfortable enough to use daily and rowdy enough to keep you grinning.
bikes.notes: 2005 private £3350 / dealer £4200, rising to 2010 private £4100 / dealer £5150

bikes.description: A triple-powered sports tourer with a single-sided swingarm and genuine long-distance ability. One of the most underrated bikes Triumph has made, and cheap for what it offers.
bikes.notes: Private sales £1875-£3450; dealer stock £2995-£3995

bikes.description: A 2.3-litre triple, the largest production motorcycle engine ever made. Absurd torque, immense physical presence and a party trick nothing else can match. Handling is, unsurprisingly, a compromise.
bikes.notes: 2006 Classic with 29k miles £4995; low-mileage 2006 £6499

bikes.description: High pipes, a torquey parallel twin and just enough off-road pretence to be charming. Never a serious dirt bike, always a lovely thing to potter about on. Values hold up well.
bikes.notes: Range £3900-£6000; 2006 part-exchange c.£3600. Depreciation has flattened

bikes.description: A triple in a class of fours, and a revelation. Midrange the Japanese 600s couldn't match, a chassis that flattered everyone, and a soundtrack to die for. One of the great modern supersports.
bikes.notes: Early private £3200, dealer from £3800; 2012 dealer c.£5650

bikes.description: A road-biased big Tiger with the Sprint's triple. Fast, comfortable and thoroughly capable on tarmac, provided you accept it has no genuine off-road ambitions whatsoever.
bikes.notes: High-mileage c.£3000; typical 2007-2013 listings £3290-£3950, most with panniers

bikes.description: The air-cooled Hinckley Bonnie. Simple, handsome and full of character, with a huge accessory catalogue and a following to match. The bike that proved retro could be done properly.
bikes.notes: Budget £4000-£4500 for the 865; top of the Bonnie market c.£5500

bikes.description: A café racer straight from the factory, with clip-ons, rearsets and a lovely stance. Slower than it looks, but few bikes look this good standing still. Values are firm.
bikes.notes: Original Thruxton 900 from c.£4500; cost £7699 new in 2013

bikes.description: The oil-cooled GS that turned the model into a phenomenon. Lighter than the bike before it, hugely capable and comfortable enough for continents. Check the final drive and spec carefully.
bikes.notes: Has depreciated further than expected: 2004 with 27.5k miles £2850, 2010 Adventure with 58k £3990

bikes.description: A middleweight GS with genuine off-road ability. Lighter and more willing in the dirt than the boxer, with a characterful parallel twin. The sensible adventure choice.
bikes.notes: Well-used from £2999; tidy with panniers £4500-£5000; top c.£5999

bikes.description: BMW's attempt at a hyper-sports tourer, with a transverse four and Duolever front end. Enormously fast and deeply odd to ride at first. Superb value now if the history is right.
bikes.notes: Listings £1750-£3995, most £2800-£3500. Has fallen further than expected

bikes.description: The default long-distance BMW. Boxer torque, electric screen, superb weather protection and the ability to cover 600 miles without complaint. Ex-police examples are cheap.
Pierre Terblanche's much-argued-about design, hiding a genuinely brilliant road bike. Torquey, agile and comfortable, if not remotely an off-roader. Cheap because of the styling.
bikes.notes: UK listings sparse; most comparables are overseas, so treat with caution

bikes.description: The Monster made accessible. Light, low and friendly, with enough of the family character to feel special. A superb first Ducati and an easy bike to live with.
bikes.notes: Sweet spot £3000-£4500; 2009 with 19k miles £3350, low-mileage 2008 £4250

bikes.description: The bike that brought Ducati's superbike back to the top. Brutal torque, gorgeous lines and a single-sided swingarm that echoed the 916. A future classic, already appreciating.
bikes.notes: Standard 1098 £5499-£7795; the £17-21k results are 1098R variants, not the base bike

bikes.description: A supermoto for the road with wide bars, a torquey air-cooled twin and terrible manners in the best possible way. Enormous fun on a back road, tiring anywhere else.
bikes.notes: 1100S listings £5590-£6240; base 1100 sits below that

bikes.description: The adventure bike for people who actually go off road and mean it. Long travel, huge ability and a V-twin with real bite. Demanding, thirsty and hugely rewarding.
bikes.notes: Well-used early bikes £4500-£5000 at a dealer; 2008-2012 listings £3999-£6750

bikes.description: The Beast. A big V-twin, minimal bodywork and a chassis that begs for trouble. KTM's naked bike at its most uncompromising and most entertaining.
bikes.notes: 2006 with 12k miles £3995; 2010 with 5k miles £4999; modified examples higher

bikes.description: Aprilia's V-twin superbike, built to fight Ducati and rather better value now. Strong, characterful and beautifully made, with a chassis good enough to embarrass fours.
bikes.notes: 1998 rough £1500-1900, tidy £2300-3200, mint £3500-4500. Best-value used litre bike

bikes.description: The RSV with the fairing removed and the bars raised, which turned out to be the best thing Aprilia ever did. Savage, loud and gloriously unhinged. A genuine cult classic.
bikes.notes: Dealers price a good one £3500-£5500; Factory models £4000-£6000

bikes.description: The bigger Sportster, and a much better bike than the 883 for barely more money. Still crude, still limited, still enormously characterful. Buy on condition and enjoy the noise.
bikes.notes: Listings £3999-£10000, most £5500-£8495; 2010s models at the top

bikes.description: A liquid-cooled, Porsche-developed V-twin in a Harley. Purists hated it, which was rather the point. Fast, distinctive and now a bargain slice of Milwaukee heresy.
bikes.notes: eBay UK bands cluster under £5560 and £5560-£11100

bikes.description: Erik Buell's oddball engineering — fuel in the frame, oil in the swingarm, rim-mounted brake disc. A Harley motor in a genuinely clever chassis. Flawed, fascinating and cheap.
bikes.notes: UK dealer c.£4490; wider listings £3384-£4497

bikes.description: One of the best-looking naked bikes ever made, with a four-cylinder howl to match. Exquisite detailing and genuine exclusivity, tempered by servicing costs and patchy dealer support.
A small-block Guzzi twin in a handsome retro package. Slow, charming and utterly relaxing, with that characteristic sideways lurch on the throttle. A bike for enjoying the journey.
bikes.notes: Listings £3698-£5999; 2008 with 6k miles £3698

bikes.description: A living fossil, and none the worse for it. Slow, simple and thumping, the Bullet asks you to adjust your expectations and rewards you with genuine charm. Cheap to buy and fix.
bikes.notes: Wide spread on eBay UK: £930, £1500, £1900 up to £4500 by age and condition

bikes.description: The Bandit grown a little more civilised, with a liquid-cooled motor and better brakes. Still a bargain, still endlessly practical, still slightly prone to corrosion.
The faired CB500, and the sensible sporty A2 choice. Enough performance to enjoy, enough comfort to commute, and Honda dependability throughout. Unexciting in the way that keeps working.
bikes.notes: 2014 with 23k miles £2990; 2019 with 5.8k miles £5290

bikes.description: The adventure-styled 500 and the pick of the family. Taller bars, longer travel and a genuinely comfortable riding position make it the most usable of the three. A superb small tourer.
bikes.notes: 2020-21 examples £4499-£4895; earlier bikes below that

bikes.description: A FireBlade motor in a single-sided-swingarm naked chassis. Handsome, strong and rather overlooked next to the European competition, which keeps used prices sensible.
bikes.notes: Private-sale guide £3750 (2009) rising to £5700 (2017); listings £3795-£4990

bikes.description: The FireBlade at its most refined. Less shouty than a BMW or an Aprilia, but beautifully balanced and easy to ride quickly. C-ABS models are heavy but effective.
A four-cylinder middleweight that prioritised usability over outright pace. Smooth, comfortable and dependable, with that inline-four noise the twins can't offer.
bikes.notes: 2015 higher-mileage £3989 up to £5395 for a tidy 2018

bikes.description: A tiny bike with an enormous personality. Twelve-inch wheels, a four-speed box and more fun per mile than almost anything. The aftermarket is vast and the grin factor is off the scale.
cons: Motorway is out of the question

bikes.description: A proper little trail bike with road manners. Light, forgiving and genuinely capable on green lanes, with Honda reliability underneath. An ideal first off-roader.
bikes.notes: Bottom of the market c.£2500 for a 2012, rising to £5000 for a 2020. Values held up remarkably

bikes.description: The V4 returns, smoother and better equipped than the VTEC bike before it. Traction control, heated grips and that glorious engine note. A wonderful sports tourer that deserved to sell better.
bikes.notes: 2014 dealer £5900 / private £4700; £6000 buys c.10k miles with full luggage

bikes.description: A low, light bobber-styled cruiser on the CB500 platform. Easy to ride, A2 legal and genuinely stylish, with a big following among newer riders.
A proper little naked bike rather than a scaled-down toy. Sharp chassis, decent brakes and enough attitude to keep a learner entertained until they can move up.
bikes.notes: 2020 with higher mileage £2400; 2023 examples to £4600. New MT-125 ABS £5300

bikes.description: The MT family's entry point, and a genuinely likeable little bike. Light, willing and sharply styled, with enough poke to be entertaining on a back road.
bikes.notes: 2016-19 well-used from £2400, nice examples £3000-£3400; later bikes higher

bikes.description: A small sportsbike that behaves like a proper one. The twin revs happily, the chassis is genuinely good, and it makes a superb track-day starter as well as a first bike.
bikes.notes: 2015 with 28k miles £1800; recent low-mileage examples £5500+

bikes.description: The MT-07 with a fairing, a bigger tank and a more upright stance. All the CP2 charm with real-world practicality bolted on. One of the best-value do-everything bikes going.
An MT-09 in a beautifully judged retro suit. The triple is as brilliant as ever, the finish is a cut above, and it looks better every year. A modern classic in waiting.
Yamaha stripped the adventure bike back to what riders actually wanted — the CP2 twin, long travel, minimal electronics and genuine off-road ability. An instant classic that holds value fiercely.
bikes.notes: eBay examples £4999-£9995; dealer stock c.£7500 upward. New 2025 £10108

bikes.description: Yamaha's big shaft-drive tourer, and a bike that eats continents. Smooth, immensely strong and comfortable for hours. Ex-police examples make superb value if the history stacks up.
bikes.notes: Older high-mileage from c.£1800-£2250; 2014 AE with 21k miles £6500

bikes.description: The GSX-R grown more civilised without losing its edge. Strong, dependable and cheaper than equivalent Japanese rivals, which makes it one of the best superbike bargains available.
bikes.notes: Nudged up: inventory holds 2014 and 2016 examples at £7499-£8499

bikes.description: A GSX-R750-derived motor in a naked chassis, sold for sensible money. Torquey, characterful and rather overlooked, which keeps it cheap on the used market.
bikes.notes: Top nudged up: a 2020 GSX-S750 Z at £6499

bikes.description: The second-generation V-Strom 650, better in almost every way and still absurdly practical. Traction control, better economy and the same indestructible V-twin. The sensible choice, again.
A light, friendly naked twin that replaced the ER-6n and improved on it. Easy to ride, cheap to run and well suited to newer riders stepping up.
The small Ninja that finally got serious. Light, quick for the class and genuinely good in the corners, it dominated club racing and made a superb first sportsbike.
bikes.notes: 2023 with 4.5k miles £3990; 2024 with 1071 miles £5999

bikes.description: A Z1000 with a fairing and panniers, which turned out to be exactly what everyone wanted. Fast, comfortable and practical, and one of the great real-world bikes of the last fifteen years.
A modern Z900 dressed as a 1972 Z1, and beautifully done. The paint, the tank shape and the exhaust note all land perfectly. Values have held up remarkably well.
bikes.notes: 2020 with 8.7k miles £7495; 2023 with 5.9k £8799; 2024 Yellow Ball £9295

bikes.description: A Z1000 motor in a tall, comfortable touring chassis. Fast, practical and thoroughly road-biased, with no off-road pretensions at all. A capable and undervalued mile-eater.
A cruiser built around adjustable ergonomics, so it fits riders of almost any size. The ER-6 twin gives it more usable performance than most cruisers manage.
bikes.notes: Search returned mainly new and near-new stock (£6728-£6779); little data on older used examples

bikes.description: More capacity, more midrange and a chassis honed to a fine point. The 765 is arguably the best middleweight naked ever built, and the RS version borders on a supersport bike with bars.
bikes.notes: Widened: Webbs hold eight at £7799-£11995. RS spec drives the top

bikes.description: The big liquid-cooled Bonnie, with torque the 900 can only dream of. Beautifully finished, genuinely comfortable and every inch the modern classic done properly.
bikes.notes: 2021 with 9.2k miles c.£8700; 2022 £9150; 2024 with 2.5k £10000. Seed was too low

bikes.description: A factory bobber with a hidden monoshock and a genuinely clever adjustable seat. Looks fantastic, rides better than it has any right to, and holds value strongly.
pros: better than it looks to ride
bikes.notes: Nudged up: a main dealer example at £14295 sits well above our previous top

bikes.description: The Bonneville engine in a sportier chassis with better brakes and suspension. Quick, handsome and hugely satisfying — arguably the best of the modern classic Triumphs.
bikes.notes: Widened: Webbs stock £6999-£14795, the top being current RS models

bikes.description: The 900 twin with high pipes and a bit of trail styling. Light, easy and genuinely charming, with just enough capability for a gravel track.
bikes.notes: 2018 with 10.5k miles £6200; 2024 with 1290 miles £8100

bikes.description: A boxer roadster built for customisation, with beautiful build quality and genuine presence. The air-cooled twin is full of character and values have stayed remarkably strong.
bikes.notes: 2014-15 £7299-£7999; 2022-23 £9695-£11999. Values holding unusually well

bikes.description: The S1000RR stripped of its fairing and given usable bars. Savagely quick, well equipped and comfortable enough to use daily. Enormous performance for the money used.
bikes.notes: 2014 stock c.£6000, Sport c.£7000; 2017-on £8000-£11500. Sport spec matters - it cannot be retrofitted

bikes.description: BMW's small single, built in India and aimed at new riders. Well finished and easy to ride, though it feels expensive next to the Japanese competition.
ShiftCam variable valve timing gave the boxer real low-down urgency, and the rest of the GS package was already the class benchmark. The default big adventure bike, still.
bikes.notes: Widened: CMC hold two at £14499-£14799, above our previous £13500 top

bikes.description: The middleweight Panigale, and far more usable than the 1299. Gorgeous, savage and just about manageable on the road. Servicing costs are the price of admission.
The Monster grown properly muscular. Torquey, handsome and genuinely quick, with the trellis-frame character intact. A big naked with real Italian presence.
bikes.notes: Base examples from c.£4475; 1200S 2015 £7300-£7995

bikes.description: Four bikes in one, courtesy of switchable riding modes that genuinely change the character. Fast, comfortable and hugely capable on road, if never a true off-roader.
A power cruiser that actually handles. Testastretta torque, a 240-section rear tyre and genuinely startling pace. Unlike any other cruiser on sale.
The Beast, fully grown. Enormous torque, a chassis that shrinks around you and absolutely no interest in restraint. One of the most exciting bikes on sale, used or new.
The biggest single you can buy, and a wonderfully odd thing. Light, torquey and hilarious in town, with a chassis that flatters. Vibration is part of the deal.
bikes.notes: 2019 with 5k miles £3499; 2012 with 7k miles £3995; 2015 with 7k miles £4750

bikes.description: A small sportsbike with genuine racetrack intent. Sharp, light and quick for the class, with a chassis that punches well above its price. A superb track-day starter.
The Scalpel. A superb parallel twin, a chassis that changes direction telepathically and electronics that actually help. One of the best-judged bikes KTM has made.
bikes.notes: Range £3999-£7999, average c.£5500 at c.4200 miles

bikes.description: A narrow-angle V4 in a chassis with more adjustment than most race bikes. Glorious noise, brilliant handling and genuine exclusivity. Dealer support is the thing to check.
bikes.notes: Top raised: a 2020 RSV4 1100 Factory at £13999. Factory and 1100 models sit well above base bikes

bikes.description: The RSV4 with bars, which is as close to a perfect road bike as the class gets. Savage, brilliantly balanced and endlessly rewarding. Widely considered the best super naked of its era.
bikes.notes: 2015 with 19k miles £6790; 2020 Factory £10790. Guide range £7000-£9000

bikes.description: A three-cylinder supersport of extraordinary beauty, with a counter-rotating crank and a soundtrack to match. Exquisite and demanding in equal measure.
bikes.notes: Values far stronger than expected: 2021 with 4885 miles £9000, 2015 with 7k miles £11480

bikes.description: A proper parallel twin retro at a price nobody could argue with. Smooth, charming and well made, it changed how the market saw Royal Enfield overnight.
bikes.notes: 2021 with 13.2k miles £3000; 2024 with 7.3k £4300; low-mileage 2024 £4699

bikes.description: A small, simple adventure bike built for rough roads rather than showroom posing. Slow, tough and genuinely capable, with a following built on honesty rather than spec.
bikes.notes: Search returned mainly dealer and near-new stock (£4999-£6499); little clean used data for the 411

bikes.description: A KTM 390 Duke in Scandinavian clothing, and rather more appealing for it. Light, sharp and distinctive, with styling that stands apart from everything else in the class.
A liquid-cooled V-twin cruiser that actually goes and stops. Smooth, quick and beautifully finished, and a genuine alternative to the Milwaukee default.
bikes.notes: 2018 with 12.6k miles £9489; 2022 with 2k £9600; up to c.£12499. Seed was too low

bikes.description: A bigger small-block Guzzi with more torque and the same laid-back charm. Handsome, relaxing and utterly unhurried. A bike for enjoying the countryside slowly.
bikes.notes: 2017 with 5.9k miles £5295; 2019 with 1.9k £5395. Slow sales have deflated values

bikes.description: An enormous amount of adventure bike for very little money. Heavy and slow, but well equipped and genuinely comfortable. The budget choice that sold in real numbers.
Kawasaki's superbike at its most successful, with the WSBK titles to prove it. Savage, focused and better mannered than the early bikes. Superb value used.
bikes.notes: 2012 with 16k miles £6189; 2016 £6995; 2018 KRT with 2.2k miles £9990

bikes.description: A GSX-S1000 wearing a modern take on the 1981 Katana's shape. Strong K5-derived motor, decent chassis and a genuine talking point, if not quite the icon the original was.
bikes.notes: 2019 with 10k miles c.£6500, under 5k miles £6700-£7000; dealer asks to £8999

bikes.description: A road-going Tiger with a fairing and touring intent. The triple is characterful, the comfort is real, and it's consistently cheaper than the German alternatives.
bikes.notes: 2013 with 25k miles £3550; 2020 with 10k miles £7350; £9500 tops it with full luggage

bikes.description: A maxi-scooter crossed with an adventure bike, with DCT and genuine off-road pretensions. Utterly odd and surprisingly convincing once you stop laughing.
bikes.notes: 2018-19 dealer stock £7500-£8300; recent examples £10990-£12699

bikes.description: Honda rediscovering how to build an exciting middleweight. A punchy parallel twin, low weight and a keen price undercut almost everything. The Hornet name finally means something again.
bikes.notes: 2023 with 5.8k miles £6499; typical £6000-£7000

bikes.description: More capacity, more torque and a much better dash. The 1100 fixed the original's main complaint without losing the off-road ability that made its name. DCT remains genuinely good.
bikes.notes: 2020-22 from £9289 with 4.7k miles; low-mileage recent examples £13300-£15900

bikes.description: Africa Twin mechanicals in a dedicated road-touring package. Comfortable, well equipped and effortlessly capable over distance. A quietly excellent tourer that deserves more attention.
The Transalp name revived on the Hornet's parallel twin. Light for the class, genuinely capable on a green lane and priced well below the European competition.
Africa Twin torque in a low, long cruiser. Smooth, quick and unusually competent for the class, with DCT available for effortless town work.
The CRF250L grown a little and improved throughout. Light, forgiving and genuinely capable on the rough stuff, with Honda dependability as standard.
bikes.notes: 2022 with 6.3k miles £4695; 2025 examples c.£4499

bikes.description: The third-generation MT-09 finally got the chassis and suspension the engine always deserved. Sharper, better damped and still gloriously rowdy. A superb super naked.
The MT-07 restyled and lightly improved, with better brakes and a stiffer frame. The CP2 twin remains one of the great engines at any price.
Not an R6 replacement but its own thing — a CP2 twin in a sharp sportsbike chassis. Slower than the old 600s and far more usable on the road.
cons: Not as fast as an R6
bikes.notes: 2022 with 2.5k miles £7290; range to c.£9500

bikes.description: The Tracer with semi-active suspension, panniers and cruise control as standard. Fast, comfortable and genuinely well equipped. One of the best sports tourers you can buy.
An R1 crossplane motor in a naked chassis, with the noise to match. Savagely quick, well equipped and one of the most characterful big nakeds on sale.
Suzuki's return to form. A new parallel twin with a 270-degree crank, proper electronics and a keen price. Sharp, characterful and a genuine rival to the Hornet and Duke.
bikes.notes: 2024 examples £5990-£6090; strong value against a c.£8000 new price

bikes.description: The V-Strom finally given genuine off-road intent, with a 21-inch front wheel and long travel. Capable, comfortable and much more convincing in the dirt than its predecessors.
bikes.notes: 2025 with 4.3k miles £6999 - roughly a third off the £10499 launch price

bikes.description: A K5-derived motor in a sports touring package with proper luggage and cruise control. Fast, comfortable and considerably cheaper than the European alternatives.
bikes.notes: Range £6500-£10300; 2025 with 1.2k miles £8999. GT+ with panniers commands a premium

bikes.description: The third-generation Busa, with proper electronics at last and the same absurd character. Effortlessly fast, beautifully finished and every inch an icon.
The Z1000SX refined further, with cruise control, a quickshifter and better wind protection. Still one of the most complete real-world motorcycles you can buy.
A Z650 dressed as a 1970s Z, and beautifully judged. Light, easy and genuinely handsome, with retro charm that doesn't cost performance.
A four-cylinder 400 that revs to 16,000rpm and screams like a 1990s 250. Utterly mad, wonderfully characterful and a joy on track.
bikes.notes: Too new for a deep UK used market; European used from c.EUR7990, new UK £7699-£8799

bikes.description: Triumph's accessible triple, and a superb piece of judgement. Characterful, well finished and priced to fight the Japanese twins. One of the best-value bikes on sale.
bikes.notes: Widened: Webbs stock £6499-£7945. Floor kept for private sales

bikes.description: The 800 replaced with a new triple and a T-plane crank that gives it a twin-like character off road. Rally versions are genuinely capable in the dirt.
Lighter, sharper and far more powerful than the 1050 it replaced. Ohlins, Brembo Stylema and a triple that pulls savagely. The Speed Triple at its most serious.
The Trident triple in a faired touring chassis. Comfortable, well priced and genuinely useful, with enough character to keep the miles interesting.
A small single built with Bajaj and priced to shock. Well finished, genuinely fun and far better made than the price suggests. A superb A2 or first big bike.
The Daytona name on the Trident triple, in a comfortable sports chassis. Not a track weapon, but a lovely road sportsbike with real character.
bikes.notes: Widened after dealer cross-check: Webbs hold four at £6499-£8995, above our previous £7600 top

bikes.description: Lighter, more powerful and sharper than the 1250, with a new frame and radar options. The GS reinvented again, and still the class benchmark.
bikes.notes: TE from c.£15995 with 8.4k miles; well-specced examples £19000-£20995

bikes.description: A comfortable, well-equipped middleweight sports tourer with a characterful parallel twin. Practical, easy to live with and a sensible alternative to the litre bikes.
An enormous 1800cc boxer in a retro cruiser chassis. The engine is a spectacle in itself, the styling is beautifully done, and the handling is exactly what you'd expect.
An S1000RR motor in a tall, comfortable touring chassis. Ferociously fast and genuinely comfortable, with the vibration issues of the early bikes largely resolved.
A V4 in the Multistrada, with radar cruise control and genuine long-distance ability. Fast, comfortable and extraordinarily well equipped. The technology flagship.
bikes.notes: V4S from £12499; 2023 with 6.2k miles £16795, with 9.1k £19495

bikes.description: A Panigale V4 with bars and winglets, which is every bit as unhinged as that sounds. Savage, beautiful and utterly uncompromising.
bikes.notes: Standard V4 from £12500; V4S 2023 £17495-£19495. SP variants higher again

bikes.description: The usable Panigale. A superb twin, gorgeous bodywork and a chassis that flatters on road and track alike. The V4's more approachable sibling.
bikes.notes: Listings found but no usable prices; 34 on Autotrader nationally. Estimate retained and flagged

bikes.description: Ducati's proper off-road adventure bike, with a 21-inch front and genuine dirt ability. Handsome, capable and a real departure from the Multistrada formula.
bikes.notes: Thin used market; pre-registered examples c.£15995 against £17471 new

bikes.description: A middleweight adventure bike with a low-slung tank and real off-road ability. Light, quick and genuinely rally-capable in R form.
bikes.notes: 2021 with 14.5k miles £5499; 2023 with 2k £7750. Depreciated far harder than seeded

bikes.description: An enormous V-twin adventure bike with radar cruise and genuine touring ability. Fast, comfortable and far more capable off road than the size suggests.
The RS660 with bars, and arguably the better road bike. Light, quick and superbly equipped, with a chassis that makes British roads a delight.
bikes.notes: Fast Bikes quotes £4999-£7999 for 2021-on

bikes.description: A genuinely off-road-focused middleweight adventure bike with long travel and a 21-inch front. Light, capable and rather overlooked next to the Italian competition.
bikes.notes: 2022 with 2.1k miles £7495; higher-mileage examples c.£6990. New £10244

bikes.description: Harley's genuinely surprising adventure bike, with a strong Revolution Max V-twin and adaptive ride height that actually works. Far better than the sceptics expected.
The Sportster reinvented around the Revolution Max motor. Quicker and better handling than the old 883, if lacking some of its raw charm.
pros: Much quicker than the old Sportster
cons: less character than the air-cooled bikes

bikes.description: A flat-track-inspired naked with a strong V-twin and genuine presence. Distinctive, characterful and now good value as the initial hype has settled.
The 650 twin in a proper cruiser chassis, with Showa forks and genuine comfort. Relaxed, handsome and priced far below the competition.
bikes.notes: 2023 with 5.8k miles £4199; typical £4489-£4595

bikes.description: A small, light roadster with real charm and a price that undercuts everything. Easy to ride, well finished and genuinely fun in town.
bikes.notes: Median £3347 across 2023-25; range £2795-£3699 against £3899 new

bikes.description: A well-equipped retro roadster at a keen price, using a KTM-derived twin. Better finished than the badge suggests and a genuine budget alternative.
bikes.notes: 2025 Sport with 3.4k miles £4199 against £6299 new. Residuals are weak

bikes.description: A premium electric naked with genuinely startling acceleration and almost no maintenance. Range remains the limiting factor, and used values have fallen hard — which makes them interesting.
bikes.notes: 2023 SR/F with 7000 miles £6495; 2023 SR with 1655 miles £7600. Seed of £8-13k was too high

bikes.description: An electric maxi-scooter that looks like a concept bike and works brilliantly in a city. Quick, quiet and genuinely practical for urban commuting.
bikes.notes: Used listings £5689 and £7399 (Avant-garde pack); £11700 new

bikes.description: The Monster with an aluminium frame instead of the trellis, which upset purists but produced a much better bike. Light, quick and far easier to ride than its predecessors.
The bike that answered the CB750 and beat it. Four cylinders, double overhead cams and 900cc when that was enormous. The Z1 is a cornerstone of motorcycling history and priced accordingly.
bikes.notes: Private 1972 £22150 down to 1976 £11600; dealer prices higher

bikes.description: That four-into-one exhaust sweep is one of the loveliest things ever bolted to a motorcycle. Small, sweet-revving and beautifully proportioned, the CB400F is a genuine design classic.
bikes.notes: Range £2800-£6000, rideable c.£3000. Auction median £2530

bikes.description: The Kettle. A water-cooled two-stroke triple that hisses and smokes its way down the road like nothing else. Smooth, torquey for a stroker and hugely characterful.
bikes.notes: Editorial £7000-£12500

bikes.description: A parallel twin that outlasted the British bikes it copied, and a favourite of the custom scene. Torquey, simple and endlessly modifiable, which is why so few remain standard.
bikes.notes: Good authentic roadsters under £5000; tidy customs c.£7000

bikes.description: Honda's gear-driven-cam V4 flagship, built to win endurance races and sold in small numbers. Heavy and complex, but magnificent to look at and increasingly collectable.
bikes.notes: Little firm UK data; collector interest rising, prices vary widely

bikes.description: The first RR, and a much sharper thing than the F it replaced. MotoGP-inspired styling, a centre-up exhaust and a chassis that took the class racing. Superb value now.
bikes.notes: Private £2500-£3000, dealers £3300-£4000. Check hard for track use

bikes.description: The 636 that gave Kawasaki an unfair advantage in a 600 class. Extra capacity meant real midrange, and the chassis was sharp enough to use it. A cracking budget supersport.
bikes.notes: UK and near-market listings £3210-£4710; European comparables from c.£2400

bikes.description: The R6 at its most ferocious, with a claimed redline that caused a certain amount of legal argument. Sharp, light and utterly focused on revs.
A sharp, light 600 from the era when the class was at its peak. Strong brakes, a willing motor and a chassis that flatters. Now genuinely cheap for the performance.
bikes.notes: 2006 with 20k miles £3400 up to £5495 for a low-mileage 2008

bikes.description: Triumph's attempt at a Japanese-style 600, undermined at launch by poor fuelling. Sort that and the chassis is genuinely good. Cheap because of the reputation.
bikes.notes: Listings £1300-£2390; even excellent examples barely break £3000

bikes.description: A big V4 tourer with shaft drive and optional DCT. Smooth, fast and beautifully built, but heavy and thirsty, which kept sales modest and used prices low.
bikes.notes: Dealers £4000-£5000 at c.30k miles, £5500 at c.20k; 2015 with 16k miles £6395. DCT rarely adds value

bikes.description: A ZZR1400 motor in a full touring chassis with shaft drive and hard luggage. Enormously fast and genuinely comfortable, if rather heavy in town.
bikes.notes: Well-used c.£4000, tidy £5000-£6000; 2014-17 examples c.£6995

bikes.description: The FireBlade finally given proper electronics and Ohlins semi-active suspension. Sharper, lighter and far more competitive, if still down on outright power against the Europeans.
bikes.notes: 2019 with 10.2k miles £10489; with 8.4k miles £13190. Seed was too low

bikes.description: The crossplane R1 with MotoGP-derived electronics and a soundtrack unlike any other litre bike. Focused, fast and genuinely special. One of the great modern superbikes.
bikes.notes: High-mileage c.£10000, tidy low-mileage c.£11500, 2019 tops out c.£14000. R1M starts £13500

bikes.description: A two-stroke 125 with genuine race-replica looks and a powerband that taught a generation to ride. The learner-legal bike everyone actually wanted.
bikes.notes: Older bulbous-fairing bikes £1500-£2000 at dealers; RSV-style from £2000 to £3500

bikes.description: The best-built learner sportsbike, with a proper aluminium frame and styling lifted from the R6. Holds value fiercely and deserves to.
bikes.notes: 2012-2017 bikes £2000-£3399; newer examples £4495+ at dealers

bikes.description: A dependable little sportsbike that taught thousands to ride. Not quick, not exciting, but utterly reliable and cheap to run — which is exactly the brief.
A learner bike with genuine attitude. Sharp chassis, strong brakes and styling borrowed from the bigger Dukes. The most grown-up-feeling 125 on the market.
The lightest 125 sportsbike, with keyless ignition and genuinely sporty handling. Quick for the class thanks to its low weight.
The default commuter scooter, and deservedly so. Frugal, reliable, comfortable and cheap to run. Thousands of delivery riders can't all be wrong.
A proper Vespa with enough performance for real roads. Steel monocoque, timeless styling and residuals that shame most motorcycles.
bikes.notes: Used listings £2995-£4299; new HPE Super lists at £6300

bikes.description: A maxi-scooter that genuinely works as transport. Comfortable, quick enough for dual carriageways and with storage for two helmets.
A premium mid-size scooter with an electric screen and genuine touring ability. Smooth, well finished and superb for longer commutes.
bikes.notes: Dealer stock £4199-£4249 with c.6k miles

bikes.description: The solid-wheeled Softail that became a cultural icon. Heavy, slow-steering and utterly unmistakable. You buy one for how it looks and sounds, and that's a perfectly good reason.
bikes.notes: Wide span: 2001 at £4000, 1990 at £13995, 2024 at £18490. Year drives it more than mileage

bikes.description: A stripped-back Dyna with mini-apes and a solo seat. Simpler and lighter than most Harleys, and one of the better ones to actually ride.
bikes.notes: Available data covers only recent 114-engined bikes (£12495-£15345); older Dyna Street Bobs not well represented

bikes.description: A proper long-distance Harley with hard bags and a detachable screen. Comfortable, torquey and capable of enormous distances at a relaxed pace.
bikes.notes: 2019-21 bikes £13995-£14499; earlier examples well below that

bikes.description: A big transverse V-twin muscle bike with striking looks and real character. Slow-selling when new, which makes it a rare and interesting used buy.
bikes.notes: Editorial £4500-£8500

bikes.description: A belt-driven parallel twin sports tourer that quietly did everything well. Comfortable, economical and typically BMW in its solidity. Undervalued used.
A single-cylinder GS that's light, friendly and hard to break. Ideal for shorter riders and new adventure converts, with genuine trail ability.
A faired Bandit by another name. Comfortable, dependable and cheap, with no pretensions to sportiness despite the bodywork.
The bike that made small sportsbikes credible again. Willing twin, decent chassis and enough performance to be genuinely entertaining on a back road.
bikes.notes: Early private just over £2000, dealers c.£2500; later bikes £2700-£3500

bikes.description: The CG125's spiritual successor. Frugal beyond belief, utterly dependable and cheap to insure. The default choice for learning and commuting.
bikes.notes: Rarely drops below £2000 even at five years old; typical £2000-£2500

bikes.description: A budget Chinese sportsbike that puts new riders on the road for very little money. Adequate rather than good, but the value is undeniable.
bikes.notes: Typically advertised c.£1500; 2021 examples £1899-£1999, newer to £2918

bikes.description: The bigger Scrambler, with the air-cooled 1100 twin and considerably more torque. Handsome and characterful, if heavier and less playful than the 800.
The Rocket reborn, bigger and lighter than before with 2.5 litres and the highest torque figure of any production bike. Utterly absurd and completely compelling.
The definitive boxer tourer, with ShiftCam torque, electronic suspension and superb weather protection. The bike police forces buy because nothing does the job better.
A small adventure bike on the 390 platform. Light, well equipped and genuinely useful on rough roads, if limited by its 19-inch front on serious terrain.
cons: Limited off road by wheel size
bikes.notes: Floor lowered: two 2023 examples at £3999, just below our previous £4000 floor

bikes.description: The Neo Sports Cafe four updated with E-Clutch on some models, letting you ride without touching the clutch lever. Smooth, sharp-looking and typically well built.
bikes.notes: 2024 with 435 miles £6589, with 1152 miles £6389. New E-Clutch £7899

bikes.description: The XSR reborn with 1980s racing colours and the excellent new CP3 chassis. Faster, sharper and better looking than the bike it replaced.
The GSX-8S given a fairing and clip-ons, producing a comfortable and characterful sports tourer at a keen price.
bikes.notes: Too new for a deep used market; new c.£8999 and GSX-8S comparables £5200-£6999

bikes.description: A light, low cruiser using the Ninja 500 twin. Easy to ride, A2 legal and far more manageable than most cruisers for newer riders.
bikes.notes: Ex-demo from £4990; dealer listings £4995-£6399 against £5999 RRP

bikes.description: The naked NC, with the same frugal twin and under-tank storage. Deeply sensible, extremely cheap to run and rather more handsome than the X.
bikes.notes: 2015 with 16k miles £1799; 2014 with 18k miles £2999; 2017 with 6k miles £4150

bikes.description: A characterful V-twin naked with decent electronics and Italian styling. Overlooked next to the Tuono, which makes it good used value.
bikes.notes: 2018 with 5.9k miles £5199; 2021 examples £6290

bikes.description: A three-cylinder naked of real beauty and genuine aggression. Exquisite to look at, thrilling to ride, and demanding in terms of servicing and dealer access.
A modern British twin with beautiful lines and a troubled production history. Buy on the strength of the individual bike and its paperwork rather than the badge.
bikes.notes: Used range £8500-£13500, average c.£12000. 2010 Cafe Racer with 4518 miles £8995

bikes.description: Honda going all-out for World Superbike, with 217bhp, winglets and Ohlins semi-active suspension. Ferociously fast and utterly focused on the track.
bikes.notes: 2023 examples £17000-£17994; 2024 £22990. Depreciation is steep from a c.£25k list
