bikes.description: A British-built electric commuter styled like a 1920s boardtracker, and genuinely lovely to look at. Removable batteries mean you can charge it in a flat with no driveway. Restricted to 45mph, so it is a town bike and nothing else.
bikes.notes: Maeving approved-used stock: 2023-24 examples £2995-£3690 by battery count and mileage

bikes.description: The RM1 given the performance it always deserved. 70mph and 80 miles of range turn a town-only curio into something you can actually commute on. Still the best-finished electric bike at anything like the money.
bikes.notes: Maeving approved-used: 2025 with 1625 miles £5995; 2026 delivery-mileage £6245. New £7495

bikes.description: Harley's electric spin-off, and a seriously quick motorcycle. Instant torque, proper Showa suspension and Brembo brakes. It cost £28,750 at launch and has depreciated brutally, which is precisely why it is now interesting.
pros: enormous depreciation works in your favour
bikes.notes: EEMC 2023 example £12990; £22990 new. Reported 30-40% loss in the first two years

bikes.description: A flat-track-styled middleweight electric on LiveWire's new Arrow platform. Lighter, cheaper and far more usable around town than the One, with a claimed 80 miles of real-world range.
bikes.notes: EEMC 2024 with 124 miles £9490

bikes.description: The bike that made electric motorcycling ordinary. Naked, unfussy and almost maintenance-free, with a belt drive and no gearbox to think about. Battery size varies enormously by year, so check the kWh before the mileage.
cons: Battery capacity varies wildly by year
bikes.notes: EEMC stock: 2018 SR 14.4 with 16k miles £4290; 2022 S 14.4 with 6k miles £8990

bikes.description: A supermoto-styled electric that is light enough to be genuinely entertaining in town. Short range limits it to commuting and hooliganism, but it is very good at both.
bikes.notes: EEMC 2023 FXE 7.2 with 1419 miles £5990

bikes.description: The dual-sport Zero, with longer travel and a 19-inch front wheel. More comfortable than the S over rough surfaces, though it is no more an off-roader than most adventure bikes are.
cons: range anxiety off the beaten track
bikes.notes: Few dedicated DS listings; a 2020 DS seen at £3550. Partly derived from S-model comparables

bikes.description: An Italian electric super naked with a 21.5kWh battery and the weight to match. Ferociously quick and beautifully made, but heavy and expensive, and Energica's commercial troubles make support a real question.
cons: tiny dealer network and uncertain support
bikes.notes: Only two Energicas listed nationally; £25440 new. Range inferred from comparable EV depreciation

bikes.description: The electric commuter that undercut everything. 58mph, a retro-flavoured chassis and a price that made petrol 125s look expensive. Build quality is where the money was saved.
pros: Very cheap to buy and run
bikes.notes: TC Max used listings scarce; TSx and Wanderer seen at £1600-£1800. New TC Max £3995

bikes.description: The scooter that refused to die, built in one form or another for nearly forty years. Steel monocoque, hand-change gearbox on the older ones, and a shape that has never needed updating. Simple enough to fix on a kerb.
bikes.notes: Our own classifieds: T5 PX125 £4750, P125 ETS £3250. Wider market £2595-£4500

bikes.description: The PX with enough power to keep up with traffic and then some. The 200 is the one the rally crowd want, and prices have moved up accordingly. Still the definitive Italian scooter.
bikes.notes: Realistic 2025-26 band £4500-£6500; earlier years cluster £3500-£4900

bikes.description: Vespa's attempt at a sporting PX, with a five-port barrel and angular 1980s bodywork. Quicker than a standard 125 and increasingly collectable among people who remember them new.
bikes.notes: Our own classifieds: T5 mk1 £3500, T5 Classic PX125 £4750, Piaggio T5 Classic £3250

bikes.description: The Lambretta most people picture. Slimline panels, a smooth shaft-driven engine and a shape that defined an era. More refined than a Vespa to ride, and the mod association keeps demand strong.
cons: Italian-built bikes cost far more than Indian ones
bikes.notes: Our classifieds: LI125 Special £4750-£5950, LI Series 3 £4850. Wider guides £2000-£4000

bikes.description: The fast one. A genuine 200 with a top-end that embarrassed small motorcycles, and now among the most sought-after scooters in the world. Check provenance obsessively — there are more SX200s about than were ever built.
bikes.notes: Guides quote £9000-£22000 for the best; our own SX225 listing £4000 suggests a wide real-world spread

bikes.description: The last and most developed Innocenti Lambretta, styled by Bertone and fast enough to justify the badge. Values have roughly doubled in a decade. Indian-built SIL versions are a fraction of the price and not the same thing.
cons: Indian SIL copies confuse the market
bikes.notes: Our GP200 listing £7000; a restored example made over £11000 at H&H. Indian-built GPs far less (ours listed £3000)

bikes.description: A German design taken as war reparations and turned into the bike that taught Britain to ride. Simple, cheap and cheerful, with a two-stroke thump that everyone of a certain age recognises instantly.
pros: Very cheap to buy and run
cons: electrics are basic even by the standards of the day
bikes.notes: Our classifieds: D7 £1750, B175 £1800-£2250, Bantam £2500

bikes.description: The 250 that put a generation on the road, and later spawned a whole family of unit singles. Modest, willing and easy to own, if never remotely exciting. A sensible first British classic.
bikes.notes: Two C15s in our own classifieds, both at £1950

bikes.description: A pre-unit 350 single built for people who rode everywhere in all weather. Torquey, unhurried and genuinely tough, with the sort of easy manners that make an old bike usable rather than an ornament.
bikes.notes: Our classifieds: B31 at £2150 and £5000 - condition drives it entirely

bikes.description: The pre-unit BSA twin, and one of the great British all-rounders. Smooth for a parallel twin, comfortable over distance, and far easier to live with than its sportier siblings. That beige paint is part of the charm.
bikes.notes: Our classifieds: Golden Flash £3875, Super Rocket £4000, A10 £3875

bikes.description: The unit-construction BSA twin in sporting trim, with twin carbs and genuine pace. Later bikes fixed most of the early problems. Buy one that has had the crank and bearings sorted and enjoy it.
bikes.notes: Our classifieds: A65L £3400-£6000, Lightning £4950-£5750, A65 Lightning £4999

bikes.description: The most charismatic British single ever built. Clip-ons, a swept-back pipe and a megaphone bark that stops conversation. Genuine matching-numbers examples command serious money, and there are more 'Goldies' about than BSA ever made.
cons: difficult to start and ride slowly
bikes.notes: Auctions £7015 and £10925; dealer asks £18950-£22000. Our own listing £10500. Provenance is everything

bikes.description: The despatch rider's bike, built by the tens of thousands for the war effort and demobbed into civilian life afterwards. Slow, heavy and almost impossible to break. A cheap way into pre-war-style motorcycling.
bikes.notes: Our classifieds: M20 £1450, WM20 £4500 and £6950. Military provenance adds a lot

bikes.description: Ariel's sporting single, and one of the handsomest British bikes of the period. Well made, nicely finished and quick enough in its day. A quality machine that has always been appreciated by people who know.
bikes.notes: Two Red Hunters in our classifieds, both price-on-application; NH350 listed at £3600

bikes.description: A two-stroke twin wrapped in full enclosure, with legshields and a dashboard. Ariel's attempt to make motorcycling clean and civilised, and a commercial failure that looks visionary now.
bikes.notes: Our classifieds: Arrow £1500; two Leaders price-on-application

bikes.description: A big AJS single, mechanically all but identical to the Matchless G80 after the two firms merged. Torquey, comfortable and honest, with enough character to make slow progress enjoyable.
bikes.notes: Our classifieds: Model 18 Statesman £3750, AJS 30 £4950, 31CSR £3250

bikes.description: The Matchless heavyweight single, and the AJS Model 18's twin under a different badge. Sound, comfortable and beautifully made, with the teledraulic forks that were genuinely advanced in 1946.
bikes.notes: Our classifieds: 350 G3LS £3750, G80CS £6200

bikes.description: The connoisseur's British single. A high-camshaft 500 with a fishtail silencer and a gearchange that rewards precision. Slower than a Gold Star, more civilised than almost anything, and utterly addictive.
cons: Many have been turned into Thruxton lookalikes
bikes.notes: Listings £5495-£12000; Viper 350 scrambler £7995. Check numbers - many wear Thruxton parts

bikes.description: A Featherbed-framed twin, which means it handles better than almost anything else of its age. The engine is willing and the chassis is famous for good reason. One of the great British roadsters.
bikes.notes: Typical £5000-£7100; listings £4750-£4999 for tidy 99s

bikes.description: The sloper. A huge, slow-revving single canted forward to act as the frame's front downtube, built to haul a sidecar and family up any hill in Yorkshire. Utterly unlike anything else on the road.
bikes.notes: Listings £9995-£13950; a 1952 carried a £6000-£8000 auction estimate

bikes.description: The Bobber's more practical cousin, with pillion provision, a bigger tank and forward controls. Same torquey 1200 twin, but set up for actually going somewhere rather than posing outside a cafe.
pros: far more usable than the Bobber
cons: forward controls do not suit everyone
bikes.notes: Five in dealer stock at £11995-£13795 (recent, low-mileage); older examples sit below

bikes.description: The Speed 400 given longer travel, a 19-inch front wheel and wider bars. Light, genuinely capable on a gravel track and priced to embarrass bikes costing twice as much. Arguably the pick of the small Triumphs.
bikes.notes: Four in dealer stock at £5795-£6645 against c.£5995 new

bikes.description: A half-faired boxer sports tourer, effectively the R1200R with weather protection. Comfortable, quick enough and quietly capable, but sold in small numbers, which keeps used prices sensible.
bikes.notes: Two in dealer stock at £6999 (Sport SE spec)

bikes.description: The first crossplane MT-10, with R1 mechanics, wild styling and a soundtrack no other naked could match. Rawer and less polished than the later bike, but cheaper and arguably more characterful.
bikes.notes: Inventory: 2020 SP with 17.4k miles £10499. Base bikes below that

bikes.description: The Tracer 700 renamed and gently improved, with better wind protection and a smarter dash. Still the same superb CP2 twin and still one of the best-value all-rounders on sale.
cons: modest wind protection on the base bike
bikes.notes: Inventory: 2021 with 1.3k miles £6999; 2024 GT with 3.7k £8299

bikes.description: A learner-legal retro with the MT-125's underpinnings and far more charm. Proper upside-down forks, decent brakes and styling that shames most 125s. Holds value strongly.
bikes.notes: Inventory: 2023 with 2.7k miles £4149

bikes.description: A leaning three-wheeler that is far less peculiar to ride than it looks. The twin front wheels genuinely add grip and confidence in the wet, which is most of the British year.
bikes.notes: Inventory: 2018 with 6.2k miles £2499

bikes.description: The bigger leaning three-wheeler, and one you can ride on a car licence with the right training. Genuinely stable, properly quick enough for dual carriageways and very reassuring in poor weather.
bikes.notes: Inventory: 2026 delivery-mileage £7499; used examples below

bikes.description: The best-built 125 maxi-scooter, with real storage, a proper riding position and Yamaha reliability. Expensive next to the budget competition and worth it.
bikes.notes: Inventory: 2024 with 5.3k miles £4199

bikes.description: The sports fifty that dominated its class, with proper suspension and genuine performance for a moped. Enormous nostalgia value now.
cons: Most have been thrashed or derestricted
bikes.notes: Added during the coverage audit; priced from UK market knowledge cross-checked against our dealer and auction data where comparables existed

bikes.description: The definitive road-legal two-stroke enduro, and the bike most serious green-laners and enduro riders end up on. Light, savagely torquey and capable of climbing almost anything. TPI fuel injection from 2018 transformed the fuelling.
bikes.notes: Road-legal enduro values are driven by engine hours and year far more than mileage; range spans an older high-hours example to a recent low-hours one

bikes.description: The four-stroke 250 enduro, and the easiest of the EXC range to ride fast. Less brutal than the 300 two-stroke and far more forgiving for a rider still learning technique.
bikes.notes: Road-legal enduro values are driven by engine hours and year far more than mileage; range spans an older high-hours example to a recent low-hours one

bikes.description: The sweet spot of the EXC range for many riders — the agility of a 250 with usefully more drive. Arguably the most complete road-legal enduro you can buy.
pros: Superb balance of power and weight
bikes.notes: Road-legal enduro values are driven by engine hours and year far more than mileage; range spans an older high-hours example to a recent low-hours one

bikes.description: The big four-stroke EXC, with enough torque to lug up anything and just about enough road manners to ride there. Popular for adventure conversions and rally builds.
bikes.notes: Road-legal enduro values are driven by engine hours and year far more than mileage; range spans an older high-hours example to a recent low-hours one

bikes.description: The Husqvarna take on the 300 two-stroke enduro, sharing KTM architecture with different suspension settings and bodywork. Every bit as capable and often a little cheaper used.
bikes.notes: Road-legal enduro values are driven by engine hours and year far more than mileage; range spans an older high-hours example to a recent low-hours one

bikes.description: A friendly four-stroke enduro that flatters a developing rider. Light, tractable and typically well finished, with the same competition underpinnings as the KTM equivalent.
bikes.notes: Dealer list: 2024 FE 250 with 276 miles £6899

bikes.description: The 350 four-stroke, and for many the ideal road-legal enduro. Enough drive for anything a trail throws up without the weight of a 450.
bikes.notes: Road-legal enduro values are driven by engine hours and year far more than mileage; range spans an older high-hours example to a recent low-hours one

bikes.description: The biggest FE, with enormous torque and enough road ability to make it a genuine dual-purpose machine. A favourite base for lightweight adventure builds.
bikes.notes: Dealer list: 2025 FE 501 with 323 miles £8995

bikes.description: The Italian alternative to the Austrians, with a softer power delivery that many riders find easier in tight going. Well made and with a loyal following.
bikes.notes: Dealer list: 2026 RR 2T 300 with delivery mileage £7700

bikes.description: A four-stroke Beta enduro with Sachs suspension and a distinctly Italian feel. Capable and characterful, and usually cheaper used than the equivalent KTM.
bikes.notes: Road-legal enduro values are driven by engine hours and year far more than mileage; range spans an older high-hours example to a recent low-hours one

bikes.description: A Spanish two-stroke enduro with a long competition history, now built under KTM ownership and sharing much with the EXC. Earlier Spanish-built bikes have their own following.
bikes.notes: Road-legal enduro values are driven by engine hours and year far more than mileage; range spans an older high-hours example to a recent low-hours one

bikes.description: The four-stroke GasGas, essentially an EXC-F in red with simpler suspension and a lower price. A sensible way into a competitive enduro bike.
bikes.notes: Road-legal enduro values are driven by engine hours and year far more than mileage; range spans an older high-hours example to a recent low-hours one

bikes.description: A French two-stroke enduro with a devoted following and genuine competition pedigree. Slightly softer than a KTM and rated highly for extreme enduro.
bikes.notes: Road-legal enduro values are driven by engine hours and year far more than mileage; range spans an older high-hours example to a recent low-hours one

bikes.description: The big four-stroke Sherco, with plenty of torque and a chassis that suits fast open going. Rare in the UK, which cuts both ways on price.
bikes.notes: Road-legal enduro values are driven by engine hours and year far more than mileage; range spans an older high-hours example to a recent low-hours one

bikes.description: Yamaha's four-stroke enduro, road legal in UK trim and famously tough. Less highly strung than the Austrian competition and cheaper to keep, which wins it a lot of friends.
bikes.notes: Road-legal enduro values are driven by engine hours and year far more than mileage; range spans an older high-hours example to a recent low-hours one

bikes.description: The big WR, with strong torque and Yamaha reliability. A sensible choice for riders who want competition ability without competition running costs.
bikes.notes: Road-legal enduro values are driven by engine hours and year far more than mileage; range spans an older high-hours example to a recent low-hours one

bikes.description: Honda's road-legal enduro, built to last rather than to win. Softer and heavier than the Europeans, and correspondingly far cheaper to own over a season.
bikes.notes: Dealer list: 2016 CRF450X with 4334 miles £3899; 2024 CRF450RX £6500

bikes.description: The CRF300L with a rally fairing, bigger tank and longer travel. Genuinely useful for long green-lane days and small-scale adventure touring.
bikes.notes: Priced against the CRF300L, which the dealer lists carry at £4250-£5200

bikes.description: A big air-cooled single trail bike that has barely changed in thirty years. Simple, tough and endlessly modifiable — a favourite for budget round-the-world builds.
bikes.notes: Road-legal enduro values are driven by engine hours and year far more than mileage; range spans an older high-hours example to a recent low-hours one

bikes.description: A light, friendly trail bike aimed at newcomers rather than racers. Low seat, easy power and Kawasaki dependability make it an ideal first green-laner.
bikes.notes: Road-legal enduro values are driven by engine hours and year far more than mileage; range spans an older high-hours example to a recent low-hours one

bikes.description: A Spanish enduro built around the well-proven GasGas two-stroke engine after Rieju acquired the tooling. Capable, well specced and usually cheaper than the big names.
bikes.notes: Road-legal enduro values are driven by engine hours and year far more than mileage; range spans an older high-hours example to a recent low-hours one

bikes.description: An Italian enduro using Yamaha's WR250F engine in Fantic's own chassis. Well finished and distinctive, with the reassurance of Japanese mechanicals underneath.
bikes.notes: Dealer list: 2026 XEF 250 Enduro Trail with 1341 miles £2999

bikes.description: A Portuguese lightweight adventure bike with a SWM-sourced single and genuine off-road ability. Rare, characterful and far lighter than the mainstream adventure crowd.
pros: Very light for an adventure bike
bikes.notes: Road-legal enduro values are driven by engine hours and year far more than mileage; range spans an older high-hours example to a recent low-hours one

bikes.description: An air-cooled four-stroke enduro from before the class went highly strung. Heavy by modern standards but almost impossible to break, and still a favourite for green-laning.
bikes.notes: Road-legal enduro values are driven by engine hours and year far more than mileage; range spans an older high-hours example to a recent low-hours one

bikes.description: A boxer twin with a handlebar fairing styled by Hans Muth, built when BMW decided it wanted a sports bike. Not fast by superbike standards, but effortless over distance and beautifully engineered.
bikes.notes: Added from the reader-poll top 80; priced from UK market knowledge, cross-checked against our auction archive where comparables existed

bikes.description: The last of the classic Earles-fork boxers, with a steering damper and a level of refinement nothing else offered in 1960. A blue-chip BMW classic and priced accordingly.
cons: Earles forks feel odd at first
bikes.notes: Iconic archive: 1961 R69S with Steib sidecar £10350; 1958 R69 £5750

bikes.description: The first production desmodromic Ducati, and the start of everything that followed. Light, willing and full of character, with a single-cylinder charm the later V-twins never quite replaced.
bikes.notes: Added from the reader-poll top 80; priced from UK market knowledge, cross-checked against our auction archive where comparables existed

bikes.description: The first belt-driven Ducati V-twin, and the architectural ancestor of the 916 and everything since. Historically vital and still cheap next to the bikes it spawned.
bikes.notes: Iconic archive: 1984 Pantah 600SL £2990. Good 500SLs ask considerably more

bikes.description: The bevel-drive 900SS, and the basis of Mike Hailwood's 1978 TT win. Desmodromic, hand-built and gloriously uncompromising — among the most desirable Ducatis ever made.
bikes.notes: Iconic archive: a 1991 900SS project made £8050; genuine bevel-drive bikes are a different market entirely

bikes.description: Honda's homologation V-twin, built to beat Ducati at their own game — and it did, twice. Raw, focused and increasingly collectable as the last of the analogue Honda superbikes.
bikes.notes: Editorial £7500-£14000; SP-1/SP-2 values climbing as homologation specials

bikes.description: The Whippet. A 200cc two-stroke single in a trellis frame weighing barely 100kg, built for Japan and smuggled out by enthusiasts. Utterly unlike anything else and now a proper cult bike.
bikes.notes: Added from the reader-poll top 80; priced from UK market knowledge, cross-checked against our auction archive where comparables existed

bikes.description: A sports tourer wearing supersport clothes, and a far more comfortable proposition than the R6 that followed. Strong, dependable and now extremely cheap.
bikes.notes: Added from the reader-poll top 80; priced from UK market knowledge, cross-checked against our auction archive where comparables existed

bikes.description: Craig Vetter's factory special, with glass-fibre bodywork, a stepped seat and three pipes down one side. Credited with inventing the factory custom, and among the most collectable Triumphs of all.
bikes.notes: Added from the reader-poll top 80; priced from UK market knowledge, cross-checked against our auction archive where comparables existed

bikes.description: The Black Pig. MV's first four-cylinder road bike, deliberately made heavy and ugly so it could not embarrass the racing department. Only 135 or so were built, which makes it fabulously rare.
bikes.notes: Added from the reader-poll top 80; priced from UK market knowledge, cross-checked against our auction archive where comparables existed

bikes.description: The bike that has taught more children to ride than anything else. Automatic, shaft driven, adjustable and virtually indestructible. Values barely move because demand never stops.
pros: Perfect first bike for a child
bikes.notes: Added from the reader-poll top 80; priced from UK market knowledge, cross-checked against our auction archive where comparables existed

bikes.description: A supercharged, 200bhp road-legal superbike with a mirror-finish paint job and a soundtrack like nothing else. The track-only H2R makes 300bhp. Genuinely unlike any other production motorcycle.
bikes.notes: Added from the reader-poll top 80; priced from UK market knowledge, cross-checked against our auction archive where comparables existed

bikes.description: KTM's only superbike, with a 75-degree V-twin and origami styling that still looks futuristic. Sharp, angry and rare, with a following that keeps values firm.
bikes.notes: Added from the reader-poll top 80; priced from UK market knowledge, cross-checked against our auction archive where comparables existed

bikes.description: The fastest production bike of its day and the first Kawasaki with an aluminium perimeter frame. Big, heavy and immensely fast in a straight line — a genuine period landmark.
bikes.notes: Added from the reader-poll top 80; priced from UK market knowledge, cross-checked against our auction archive where comparables existed

bikes.description: Suzuki's long-running V-twin cruiser, sold in every capacity from 125 to 1400. Honest, cheap and dependable, if never as characterful as the American competition.
bikes.notes: Added from the reader-poll top 80; priced from UK market knowledge, cross-checked against our auction archive where comparables existed

bikes.description: The Intruder renamed and, in M109R form, given a 1.8-litre V-twin and a 240-section rear tyre. A genuine power cruiser that will out-drag most sportsbikes to sixty.
bikes.notes: Added from the reader-poll top 80; priced from UK market knowledge, cross-checked against our auction archive where comparables existed

bikes.description: A budget cruiser aimed at riders who wanted the look on an A2 licence. Basic in every respect, but cheap enough that the compromises are forgivable.
pros: cruiser styling on a small capacity
bikes.notes: Added from the reader-poll top 80; priced from UK market knowledge, cross-checked against our auction archive where comparables existed

bikes.description: An S1000RR with the first semi-active suspension fitted to a production motorcycle, plus forged wheels and titanium exhaust. A genuine technical landmark and produced in small numbers.
bikes.notes: Added from the reader-poll top 80; priced from UK market knowledge, cross-checked against our auction archive where comparables existed

bikes.description: A big air-cooled pushrod V-twin built to take the fight to Milwaukee. Torquey, simple and endlessly customisable, with a loyal following on both sides of the Atlantic.
bikes.notes: Added from the reader-poll top 80; priced from UK market knowledge, cross-checked against our auction archive where comparables existed

bikes.description: An overlooked middleweight sports tourer that stayed on sale for eighteen years. Roomy, stable and quick enough, and now about as much bike as you can buy for the money.
bikes.notes: Added from the reader-poll top 80; priced from UK market knowledge, cross-checked against our auction archive where comparables existed

bikes.description: The Fizzy. The pedal-equipped sports moped that put a generation of sixteen-year-olds on the road, and now worth many times what it cost new. Nostalgia has made it genuinely valuable.
cons: original examples are rare and pricey
bikes.notes: Iconic archive: 1974 FS1-E sold £4600, 1976 FS1 £4025, another £3105

bikes.description: Britain's answer to the CB750, badged as both the Triumph Trident and the BSA Rocket 3. A magnificent triple soundtrack, let down at the time by styling and BSA's collapse.
bikes.notes: Iconic archive: 1976 T160 Trident £5175; BSA A75R Rocket 3 £5520 and £5750

bikes.description: The final and finest development of the Venom, built in tiny numbers and a winner at the Production TT. The connoisseur's British single, and priced as such.
bikes.notes: Added from the reader-poll top 80; priced from UK market knowledge, cross-checked against our auction archive where comparables existed

bikes.description: Norton's smallest ever engine and its first unit-construction twin, built to chase the learner market. Not their finest hour mechanically, but cheap and increasingly interesting.
bikes.notes: Iconic archive: 1961 Jubilee £862, 1965 £230. Values remain very low

bikes.description: A 72-degree V-twin with Heron heads and beautiful proportions, and one of the great Italian middleweights. Sweet-handling, well engineered and still undervalued.
bikes.notes: Iconic archive: c.1974 350 Mk1 £1035; tidy Sport models list well above that

bikes.description: The Trusty. Over 30,000 were built for despatch riders in the Great War, and it did as much as anything to establish the motorcycle as serious transport. A genuine piece of history.
bikes.notes: Iconic archive: c.1919 Model H 550cc sold £4830

bikes.description: A faithful recreation of Steve McQueen's Rickman Metisse, built in a limited run of 300. Beautifully made, genuinely rideable and carrying the best backstory in motorcycling.
bikes.notes: Iconic archive: 1978 Rickman Metisse Triumph £6900. The 2009 replica run listed at £13999 new

bikes.description: The definitive British racing single, and the bike that dominated the Isle of Man for a generation. The Featherbed frame it introduced changed motorcycle chassis design permanently.
bikes.notes: Added from the reader-poll top 80; priced from UK market knowledge, cross-checked against our auction archive where comparables existed

bikes.description: A proper little motorcycle rather than a moped, with a monoshock frame and disc brake at a time when rivals had neither. Restricted to 30mph but sharp-handling and much loved.
bikes.notes: Added from the reader-poll top 80; priced from UK market knowledge, cross-checked against our auction archive where comparables existed

bikes.description: The ZZR1100's replacement, with more midrange and better manners if slightly less of the original's legend. Enormously capable over distance and now remarkably cheap for the performance on offer.
pros: very cheap for what it is
bikes.notes: Added from the best-value 50 cross-reference; priced from UK market knowledge and our dealer lists

bikes.description: The Bandit grown up, with a fuel-injected 1250 that makes its torque low down and asks nothing of you. Less frantic than the old 1200 and a superb budget all-rounder.
bikes.notes: Priced against the faired GSX1250FA, which dealer lists carry at c.£4999

bikes.description: The naked Ninja 400, and one of the best A2 bikes on sale. Light, sharp and genuinely fun, with enough quality to feel a class above the budget competition.
bikes.notes: Added from the best-value 50 cross-reference; priced from UK market knowledge and our dealer lists

bikes.description: A learner-legal cruiser sold at a price that undercuts everything. Basic in every respect, but it puts new riders on two wheels for very little money and parts are cheap.
pros: cruiser styling on an A1 licence
bikes.notes: Dealer list: 2025 Michigan 125 with 8100 miles £1400

bikes.description: A stripped-back, exposed-frame 50 that became a cult object well beyond its intended market. Mostly grey imports in the UK, with a huge customising scene behind it.
bikes.notes: Added from the best-value 50 cross-reference; priced from UK market knowledge and our dealer lists

bikes.description: The last great air-cooled Japanese muscle bike, with 1400cc of unstressed torque and the physical presence of a small car. Built in modest numbers and increasingly collectable.
bikes.notes: Added from the modern-classics 50 cross-reference; priced from UK market knowledge and our dealer lists

bikes.description: An air-cooled inline four built in the 1970s idiom but with modern metallurgy and Honda's best finish. Beautifully detailed and widely regarded as investment-grade among modern retros.
bikes.notes: Added from the modern-classics 50 cross-reference; priced from UK market knowledge and our dealer lists

bikes.description: One of the bikes that started the factory retro movement, styled after the Z1 and built when nobody else was looking backwards. Increasingly collectable and still usable daily.
bikes.notes: Added from the modern-classics 50 cross-reference; priced from UK market knowledge and our dealer lists

bikes.description: The big Zephyr, with a detuned GPZ1100 motor and proper Z1 presence. Rarer than the 750 in the UK and correspondingly sought after.
bikes.notes: Added from the modern-classics 50 cross-reference; priced from UK market knowledge and our dealer lists

bikes.description: An unfussy air-cooled four with hydraulic valve lifters, so it never needs a shim service. Built for despatch riders and riding schools, and almost impossible to wear out.
bikes.notes: Added from the modern-classics 50 cross-reference; priced from UK market knowledge and our dealer lists

bikes.description: An understated retro naked using the oil-cooled GSX-R-derived motor. Overlooked when new and still cheap, which makes it one of the better-kept secrets of the class.
bikes.notes: Added from the modern-classics 50 cross-reference; priced from UK market knowledge and our dealer lists

bikes.description: A scaled-down XJR built for the Japanese market and imported in numbers. Classic muscle-bike looks with a high-revving 400 four underneath, and A2-friendly power.
pros: Classic looks in a small package
bikes.notes: Added from the modern-classics 50 cross-reference; priced from UK market knowledge and our dealer lists

bikes.description: The Thruxton grown up, with Ohlins, Brembo and a genuinely quick 1200 twin. A café racer that actually goes and stops like a modern bike, and holds value accordingly.
bikes.notes: Added from the modern-classics 50 cross-reference; priced from UK market knowledge and our dealer lists

bikes.description: The nineT with a half fairing and low clip-ons, styled after 1970s endurance racers. Beautiful to look at, uncompromising to ride, and made in small numbers.
bikes.notes: Added from the modern-classics 50 cross-reference; priced from UK market knowledge and our dealer lists

bikes.description: A café racer built on Africa Twin mechanicals, with a bullet fairing and clip-ons. Rare in the UK and quite unlike anything else Honda currently sells.
bikes.notes: Added from the modern-classics 50 cross-reference; priced from UK market knowledge and our dealer lists

bikes.description: A road-biased Himalayan with a 19-inch front wheel and less bodywork. Simpler, lighter-feeling and cheaper, and just as easy to fix on a kerbside.
bikes.notes: Added from the modern-classics 50 cross-reference; priced from UK market knowledge and our dealer lists

bikes.description: An Italian-designed, Chinese-built scrambler with a decent parallel twin and genuine style. A2-legal and priced well below the European competition.
bikes.notes: Added from the modern-classics 50 cross-reference; priced from UK market knowledge and our dealer lists

bikes.description: The café racer sibling to the Svartpilen, with clip-ons and stark Scandinavian styling. KTM 390 mechanics underneath make it sharp and light.
bikes.notes: Added from the modern-classics 50 cross-reference; priced from UK market knowledge and our dealer lists

bikes.description: A fat-tyred retro utility bike with genuine cult status in the UK. Slow, soft and enormously likeable, with running costs close to nothing.
bikes.notes: Added from the modern-classics 50 cross-reference; priced from UK market knowledge and our dealer lists

bikes.description: A French-branded, Chinese-built learner retro that looks far more expensive than it is. Basic underneath, but a genuinely handsome way onto two wheels.
pros: Looks the part for very little
bikes.notes: Added from the modern-classics 50 cross-reference; priced from UK market knowledge and our dealer lists

bikes.description: A learner-legal café racer with an Italian badge and styling that punches far above the price. Well finished for the class and genuinely desirable.
bikes.notes: Added from the modern-classics 50 cross-reference; priced from UK market knowledge and our dealer lists

bikes.description: A simple British-branded learner café racer using proven single-cylinder tech. Cheap, easy to fix and a friendly entry point into retro biking.
bikes.notes: Added from the modern-classics 50 cross-reference; priced from UK market knowledge and our dealer lists

bikes.description: A modern reproduction of the BMW-derived Chinese military outfit, sold new with a sidecar and updated mechanicals. Utterly impractical and completely charming.
bikes.notes: Added from the modern-classics 50 cross-reference; priced from UK market knowledge and our dealer lists

bikes.description: The original Brutale, and one of Massimo Tamburini's finest shapes. A howling four-cylinder naked with exquisite detailing and the organ-pipe exhausts that became an MV signature.
cons: dealer network was thin when new
bikes.notes: Added after cross-referencing morebikes.co.uk used buyer guides; priced from UK market knowledge

bikes.description: A 848 superbike stripped of its fairing and given wide bars. Sharp, loud and considerably more usable on the road than the 1098-based original, with the same aggressive stance.
bikes.notes: Added after cross-referencing morebikes.co.uk used buyer guides; priced from UK market knowledge

bikes.description: The faired, homologation-flavoured TL, built to go World Superbike racing. Heavier and less successful than Suzuki hoped, but a strong, characterful V-twin and cheap for what it is.
bikes.notes: Added after cross-referencing morebikes.co.uk used buyer guides; priced from UK market knowledge

bikes.description: A V4 adventure-styled road bike, using the VFR800 engine in a taller chassis. Not an off-roader, but a superb all-weather all-rounder with a wonderful engine note.
bikes.notes: Added after cross-referencing morebikes.co.uk used buyer guides; priced from UK market knowledge

bikes.description: The big air-cooled XT single, and the backbone of trail riding for two decades. Simple, tough and endlessly repairable, with a following that keeps tidy examples in demand.
bikes.notes: Added after cross-referencing morebikes.co.uk used buyer guides; priced from UK market knowledge

bikes.description: Yamaha's big shaft-driven adventure bike, built to Dakar-winning heritage but aimed squarely at long-distance touring. Immensely durable and consistently undervalued against the GS.
bikes.notes: Added after cross-referencing morebikes.co.uk used buyer guides; priced from UK market knowledge

bikes.description: A mid-size V-twin cruiser with shaft drive and classic proportions. Easy to ride, cheap to own and a popular base for customs, which is where many have ended up.
bikes.notes: Added after cross-referencing morebikes.co.uk used buyer guides; priced from UK market knowledge

bikes.description: A learner-legal V-twin adventure bike that looks like the 1000 and rides like a proper motorcycle. Heavy for a 125, but comfortable and unusually grown-up.
bikes.notes: Added after cross-referencing morebikes.co.uk used buyer guides; priced from UK market knowledge

bikes.description: A V-twin two-stroke race replica with a genuine GP pedigree and a powerband that arrives like a light switch. One of the great 250 strokers and now seriously collectable.
bikes.notes: Added after cross-referencing morebikes.co.uk used buyer guides; priced from UK market knowledge

bikes.description: A naked TT600, and a much better bike than its sales suggested. The fuelling problems were sorted by then, the chassis is excellent, and it remains genuinely cheap.
bikes.notes: Added after cross-referencing morebikes.co.uk used buyer guides; priced from UK market knowledge

bikes.description: A grey-import Japanese-market four with a screaming top end and classic naked looks. A2-friendly and increasingly popular as a project base.
bikes.notes: Added after cross-referencing morebikes.co.uk used buyer guides; priced from UK market knowledge

bikes.description: The Dyna-framed Low Rider, with twin shocks and a rubber-mounted engine that makes it noticeably more comfortable than the Softails. A favourite among riders who actually cover miles.
bikes.notes: Added after cross-referencing morebikes.co.uk used buyer guides; priced from UK market knowledge

bikes.description: The Green Frame. Built to celebrate Paul Smart's 1972 Imola win, with desmodromic heads and sand-cast cases. Fewer than 500 were made and it is among the most valuable Ducatis in existence.
bikes.notes: Price taken from the editorial top-100/top-50 lists supplied 2026-08-18, which quote representative UK values for good examples rather than the full rough-to-mint spread

bikes.description: Hans Muth's smoke-orange masterpiece, with a bikini fairing, cockpit clock and hand-sprayed paint. The first genuinely sporting BMW and a cornerstone of the marque's collectability.
bikes.notes: Price taken from the editorial top-100/top-50 lists supplied 2026-08-18, which quote representative UK values for good examples rather than the full rough-to-mint spread

bikes.description: A hand-built orange endurance racer with lights. Around 550 were made and they won Oss, Barcelona and the Bol d'Or. One of the great Italian competition bikes.
bikes.notes: Price taken from the editorial top-100/top-50 lists supplied 2026-08-18, which quote representative UK values for good examples rather than the full rough-to-mint spread

bikes.description: Lino Tonti's frame wrapped around the transverse twin, in lime green with a red frame. The bike that made Guzzi a serious sporting proposition.
bikes.notes: Price taken from the editorial top-100/top-50 lists supplied 2026-08-18, which quote representative UK values for good examples rather than the full rough-to-mint spread

bikes.description: A shaft-drive four-cylinder built by a company that had just won umpteen world championships. Red, white and blue, gloriously impractical and staggeringly expensive.
bikes.notes: Price taken from the editorial top-100/top-50 lists supplied 2026-08-18, which quote representative UK values for good examples rather than the full rough-to-mint spread

bikes.description: A civilised bevel-drive Ducati with electric start, left-side gearchange and Giugiaro-influenced styling. The usable classic Ducati, and cheaper than an SS.
bikes.notes: Price taken from the editorial top-100/top-50 lists supplied 2026-08-18, which quote representative UK values for good examples rather than the full rough-to-mint spread

bikes.description: Built to celebrate Hailwood's astonishing 1978 TT comeback win. Bevel-drive desmo underneath, with the red and green livery that made it famous.
bikes.notes: Price taken from the editorial top-100/top-50 lists supplied 2026-08-18, which quote representative UK values for good examples rather than the full rough-to-mint spread

bikes.description: The world's first production six-cylinder motorcycle, with six chrome pipes fanning out across the back. More spectacle than sports bike, and all the better for it.
bikes.notes: Price taken from the editorial top-100/top-50 lists supplied 2026-08-18, which quote representative UK values for good examples rather than the full rough-to-mint spread

bikes.description: Developed with Sammy Miller, the Sherpa T rewrote observed trials and dominated the sport for a decade. Light, torquey and still competitive in classic trials.
bikes.notes: Price taken from the editorial top-100/top-50 lists supplied 2026-08-18, which quote representative UK values for good examples rather than the full rough-to-mint spread

bikes.description: The Spanish trials icon, with its slimline tank-seat unit and famously smooth low-rev delivery. A staple of classic trials paddocks.
bikes.notes: Price taken from the editorial top-100/top-50 lists supplied 2026-08-18, which quote representative UK values for good examples rather than the full rough-to-mint spread

bikes.description: The lightweight Swedish two-stroke that dominated world motocross and put Steve McQueen on the cover of Sports Illustrated. A genuine icon of off-road racing.
bikes.notes: Price taken from the editorial top-100/top-50 lists supplied 2026-08-18, which quote representative UK values for good examples rather than the full rough-to-mint spread

bikes.description: German motocrossers famous for long-travel suspension and handling that riders still talk about. The MC490 in particular was a class benchmark.
bikes.notes: Price taken from the editorial top-100/top-50 lists supplied 2026-08-18, which quote representative UK values for good examples rather than the full rough-to-mint spread
